sentences.zh: 【唐紀七十二】　起閼逢執徐六月，盡強圉協洽三月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 72] From the sixth month of Yanfeng Zhixu through the third month of Qiangyu Xiejia; more than two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 72] From the sixth month of Yanfeng Zhixu through the third month of Qiangyu Xiejia—a span of more than two years.

sentences.zh: 僖宗惠聖恭定孝皇帝下之上中和四年（

translations.literal: Below [the account of] Emperor Xizong Huisheng Gongding Xiaoxiao, Part One: Zhonghe year 4 (
translations.idiomatic: Below [the account of] Emperor Xizong, Huisheng Gongding Xiaoxiao, Part One—Zhonghe year 4 (

sentences.zh: 甲辰，公元八八四年）

translations.literal: Jiachen, equivalent to 884 CE)
translations.idiomatic: Jiachen, equivalent to 884 CE)

sentences.zh: 六月，壬辰，東川留後高仁厚奏鄭君雄斬楊師立出降。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renchen day, Gao Renhou, acting military governor of Dongchuan, memorialized that Zheng Junxiong had beheaded Yang Shili and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renchen day, Gao Renhou, acting military governor of Dongchuan, reported that Zheng Junxiong had killed Yang Shili and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 仁厚圍梓州久不下，乃為書射城中，道其將士曰：「仁厚不忍城中玉石俱焚，為諸君緩師十日，使諸君自成其功。

translations.literal: Renhou had besieged Zizhou for a long time without taking it, so he had a letter shot into the city, addressing the troops: "Renhou cannot bear to see the city and all within it burned together. I shall grant you ten days to hold back the army, that you may accomplish the deed yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: After a long siege of Zizhou that would not fall, Renhou shot a letter into the city telling the garrison: "I cannot bear to see the city destroyed with everyone in it. I will give you ten days to finish this yourselves.

sentences.zh: 若十日不送師立首，當分見兵為五番，番分晝夜以攻之，於此甚逸，於彼必困矣。

translations.literal: If within ten days you do not deliver Shili's head, I shall divide the visible troops into five shifts, each attacking day and night in turn—very easy for us here, and you there will surely be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not send Shili's head within ten days, I will divide my forces into five shifts and attack you around the clock—easy work for us, and you will be worn down.

sentences.zh: 五日不下，四面俱進，克之必矣。

translations.literal: If in five days you still do not take it, we shall advance on all four sides and capture it without fail.
translations.idiomatic: If the city has not fallen in five days, we will attack from all sides and take it for certain.

sentences.zh: 諸君圖之！

translations.literal: Consider this, all of you!
translations.idiomatic: Think it over, all of you!

sentences.zh: 」數日，君雄大呼於眾曰：「天子所誅者元惡耳，他人無預也！

translations.literal: " Several days later, Junxiong shouted to the crowd: "The Son of Heaven punishes only the chief villain; the rest of you have no part in it!
translations.idiomatic: " A few days later, Junxiong cried out to the troops: "The Son of Heaven seeks only the ringleader; the rest of you are not implicated!

sentences.zh: 」眾呼萬歲，大噪，突入府中，師立自殺，君雄挈其首出降。

translations.literal: " The crowd shouted "Long live the Emperor!" and raised a great clamor, rushed into the headquarters, Shili killed himself, and Junxiong brought out his head to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " The men shouted "Long live the Emperor!" and with a great uproar stormed the headquarters. Shili killed himself, and Junxiong brought out his head to surrender.

sentences.zh: 仁厚獻其首及妻子於行在，陳敬瑄釘其子於城北，敬瑄三子出觀之，釘者呼曰：「茲事行及汝曹，汝曹於後努力領取！

translations.literal: Renhou presented the head and Shili's wife and children to the imperial court. Chen Jingxuan had Shili's son nailed up outside the north gate; Jingxuan's three sons came out to watch, and the nailed man called out: "This will soon come to you—work hard to receive it when it does!
translations.idiomatic: Renhou sent the head and Shili's family to the emperor's camp. Chen Jingxuan had Shili's son nailed up by the north gate. Jingxuan's three sons came out to watch, and the victim shouted: "This will reach you soon—do your best to claim your share when it comes!

sentences.zh: 」三子走馬而返。

translations.literal: " The three sons galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: " The three sons wheeled their horses and fled.

sentences.zh: 以高仁厚為東川節度使。

translations.literal: Gao Renhou was appointed military governor of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Renhou was appointed military governor of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，武寧將李師悅與尚讓追黃巢至瑕丘，敗之。

translations.literal: On jiachen day, Li Shiyue, a general of Wuning, and Shang Rang pursued Huang Chao to Xiaqiu and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day, Li Shiyue of Wuning and Shang Rang pursued Huang Chao to Xiaqiu and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 巢眾殆盡，走至狼虎谷，丙午，巢甥林言斬巢兄弟妻子首，將詣時溥，遇沙陀博野軍，奪之，並斬言首以獻於溥。

translations.literal: Chao's followers were nearly wiped out; he fled to Langhu Valley. On bingwu day, Chao's nephew Lin Yan beheaded Chao, his brothers, wife, and children and set out to present the heads to Shi Pu; he encountered the Shatuo Boye Army, which seized the heads, also beheaded Yan, and presented all the heads to Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's forces were nearly gone; he fled to Langhu Valley. On bingwu day, his nephew Lin Yan cut off the heads of Chao, his brothers, wife, and children and set out to deliver them to Shi Pu. He met the Shatuo Boye Army, which seized the heads, killed Yan as well, and presented everything to Pu.

sentences.zh: 蔡州節度使秦宗權縱兵四出，侵噬鄰道。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan, military governor of Caizhou, sent his troops in all directions to raid and devour neighboring circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan, military governor of Caizhou, unleashed his troops in every direction to plunder neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 天平節度使朱瑄，有眾三萬，從父弟瑾，勇冠軍中。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan, military governor of Tianping, had thirty thousand men; his younger cousin of the same clan, Zhu Jin, was the bravest in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan, military governor of Tianping, commanded thirty thousand men. His younger cousin Zhu Jin was the bravest soldier in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 宣武節度使朱全忠為宗權所攻，勢甚窘，求救於瑄，瑄遣瑾將兵救之，敗宗權於合鄉。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong, military governor of Xuanwu, was attacked by Zongquan and in dire straits; he sought aid from Xuan, who sent Jin with troops to rescue him and defeated Zongquan at Hexiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong of Xuanwu was hard pressed by Zongquan and begged Xuan for help. Xuan sent Jin with an army, and they defeated Zongquan at Hexiang.

sentences.zh: 全忠德之，與瑄約為兄弟。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was grateful to him and swore brotherhood with Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful, Quanzhong swore brotherhood with Xuan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬午，時溥遣使獻黃巢及家人首並姬妾，上御大玄樓受之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on renwu day, Shi Pu sent envoys to present the heads of Huang Chao and his family members, along with his concubines; the emperor received them at the Da Xuan Tower.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renwu day, Shi Pu sent envoys bearing the heads of Huang Chao and his kin, together with his concubines. The emperor received them at the Da Xuan Tower.

sentences.zh: 宣問姬妾：「汝曹皆勳貴子女，世受國恩，何為從賊？

translations.literal: He questioned the concubines: "You are all daughters of meritorious noble houses, who have enjoyed the state's grace for generations—why did you follow the rebel?
translations.idiomatic: He questioned the concubines: "You are all daughters of noble houses that have served the dynasty for generations. Why did you follow the rebel?

sentences.zh: 」其居首者對曰：「狂賊凶逆，國家以百萬之眾，失守宗祧，播遷巴、蜀；

translations.literal: " The one at the front answered: "The mad rebel was violent and treacherous; the state, with its million-strong armies, lost the imperial shrines and was driven to wander in Ba and Shu;
translations.idiomatic: " The woman at the front answered: "That mad rebel was brutal and treacherous. The empire, with armies in the millions, lost the ancestral shrines and was driven into exile in Ba and Shu.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以不能拒賊責一女子，置公卿將帥於何地乎！

translations.literal: now Your Majesty blames a single woman for failing to resist the rebel—where does that leave your ministers and generals!
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty blames one woman for not resisting the rebel—where does that leave your ministers and generals!

sentences.zh: 」上不復問，皆戮之於市。

translations.literal: " The emperor asked no more questions and had them all executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked no more and had them all executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 人爭與之酒，其餘皆悲怖昏醉，居首者獨不飲不泣，至於就刑，神色肅然。

translations.literal: People vied to offer them wine; the rest were grief-stricken, terrified, and drunk with despair, but the leader alone neither drank nor wept, and at the moment of execution her bearing remained composed.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers pressed wine on them; the others wept and drank themselves into a stupor of fear, but the leader neither drank nor cried, and went to her death with a calm, solemn face.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠擊秦宗權，敗示權於殷水。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong attacked Qin Zongquan, defeated him, and displayed [the victory] at Yinshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong attacked Qin Zongquan, routed him, and paraded the captives at Yinshui.

sentences.zh: 李克用至晉陽，大治甲兵，遣榆次鎮將雁門李承嗣奉表詣行在，自陳：「有破黃巢大功，為朱全忠所圖，僅能自免，將佐已下從行者三百餘人，並牌印皆沒不返。

translations.literal: Li Keyong reached Jinyang and greatly repaired armor and weapons. He sent Li Chengsi of Yanmen, garrison commander of Yuci, to the imperial court with a memorial stating: "I had great merit in defeating Huang Chao, but was plotted against by Zhu Quanzhong and barely escaped with my life; more than three hundred officers and men who accompanied me, along with their tally-seals, were seized and never returned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong reached Jinyang and set about rearming his forces in earnest. He sent Li Chengsi of Yanmen, the garrison commander at Yuci, to the imperial court with a memorial: "I played a leading part in crushing Huang Chao, yet Zhu Quanzhong plotted against me and I barely escaped. More than three hundred officers and men who came with me, and all their tally-seals, were seized and never returned.

sentences.zh: 全忠仍榜東都、陝、孟，雲臣已死，行營兵潰，令所在邀遮屠翦，勿令潮失，將士皆號泣冤訴，請復仇讎。

translations.literal: Quanzhong also posted notices in the eastern capital, Shaan, and Meng, claiming that your subject was dead and that the field army had collapsed, ordering all places to intercept, cut down, and slaughter, that not a single man of the tide might escape; officers and soldiers all wept and pleaded their wrongs, begging to take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong also posted proclamations in the eastern capital, Shaan, and Meng claiming I was dead and my army routed, ordering every post to cut us down so that not one of my men should escape. My officers and soldiers weep and plead their innocence, begging leave to take revenge.

sentences.zh: 臣以朝廷至公，當俟詔命，拊循抑止，復歸本道。

translations.literal: Your subject, considering the court's supreme fairness, ought to await imperial command; I have soothed and restrained them and returned to my own circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Out of respect for the court's impartiality I have restrained them and awaited your orders, and have returned to my own circuit.

sentences.zh: 乞遣使按問，發兵誅討，臣遣弟克勤將萬騎在河中俟命。

translations.literal: I beg that envoys be sent to investigate, and troops dispatched for punishment; your subject has sent my younger brother Keqin with ten thousand horsemen to wait at orders in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that you send envoys to investigate and troops to punish him. I have sent my brother Keqin with ten thousand horsemen to Hezhong, awaiting your command.

sentences.zh: 」時朝廷以大寇初平，方務姑息，得克用表，大恐，但遣中使賜優詔和解之。

translations.literal: " At that time the court, having just pacified the great bandit, was intent on indulgence; receiving Keyong's memorial, it was greatly alarmed and only sent palace envoys with gracious edicts to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: " The court had only just put down the great rebellion and was bent on conciliation. Alarmed by Keyong's memorial, it sent only palace envoys with gracious edicts to patch things up.

sentences.zh: 克用前後凡八表，稱：「全忠妒功疾能，陰狡禍賊，異日必為國患。

translations.literal: Keyong submitted eight memorials in all, stating: "Quanzhong is jealous of merit and hates ability; he is a secretly treacherous bringer of calamity and will surely become a peril to the state in days to come.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent eight memorials in all, declaring: "Quanzhong envies merit and hates talent. He is a secret schemer and a source of disaster, and will one day become a grave threat to the state.

sentences.zh: 惟乞下詔削其官爵，臣自帥本道兵討之，不用度支糧餉。

translations.literal: I beg only that an edict be issued stripping him of office and rank; your subject will personally lead the troops of my circuit to attack him, without using provisions from the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: I beg only that you strip him of rank by edict. I will lead my own circuit's troops against him and will not draw on the treasury for supplies.

sentences.zh: 」上累遣楊復恭等諭指，稱：「吾深知卿冤，方事之殷，姑存大體。

translations.literal: " The emperor repeatedly sent Yang Fugong and others to convey his intent, saying: "I know well your grievance; affairs are pressing just now—let us for the moment preserve the larger interest.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor repeatedly sent Yang Fugong and others to explain: "I know full well you have been wronged, but affairs are urgent just now. For the moment, let us preserve the larger peace.

sentences.zh: 」克用終鬱鬱不平。

translations.literal: " Keyong remained resentful and ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " Keyong remained bitter and unreconciled.

sentences.zh: 時籓鎮相攻者，朝廷不復為之辨曲直。

translations.literal: At that time when military governors attacked one another, the court no longer judged right and wrong between them.
translations.idiomatic: When the military governors fought one another, the court no longer bothered to judge who was right or wrong.

sentences.zh: 由是互相吞噬，惟力是視，皆無所稟畏矣。

translations.literal: Hence they devoured one another, caring only for strength, and none feared to report or obey.
translations.idiomatic: They swallowed one another up, respecting only force, and no longer feared or obeyed the throne.

sentences.zh: 八月，李克用奏請割麟州隸河東，又奏請以弟克修為昭義節度使，皆許之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Li Keyong memorialized requesting that Linzhou be detached and placed under Hedong, and also requested that his younger brother Kexiu be made military governor of Zhaoyi; both were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Li Keyong asked that Linzhou be placed under Hedong and that his brother Kexiu be appointed military governor of Zhaoyi. Both requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 由是昭義分為二鎮，進克用爵隴西郡王。

translations.literal: Hence Zhaoyi was divided into two commands, and Keyong was advanced to Prince of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi was thus split into two commands, and Keyong was promoted to Prince of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 克用奏罷雲蔚防禦使，依舊隸河東，從之。

translations.literal: Keyong memorialized to abolish the Yunwei defense commissioner and restore it to Hedong's jurisdiction; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong asked that the Yunwei defense command be abolished and the region returned to Hedong. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 九月，己未，加朱全忠同平章事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiwei day, Zhu Quanzhong was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiwei day, Zhu Quanzhong was appointed Associate Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 以右僕射、大明宮留守王徽知京兆尹事。

translations.literal: Wang Hui, Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and keeper of the Daming Palace, was appointed to oversee the office of the metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and keeper of the Daming Palace, was put in charge of the metropolitan government of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 上以長安宮室焚毀，故久留蜀未歸。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the palaces of Chang'an had been burned, had long remained in Shu without returning.
translations.idiomatic: Because the palaces of Chang'an had been burned, the emperor had long lingered in Shu without returning.

sentences.zh: 徽招撫流散，戶口稍歸，復繕治宮室，百司粗有緒。

translations.literal: Hui gathered and comforted the scattered populace; households gradually returned; he restored the palaces, and the hundred offices roughly had order again.
translations.idiomatic: Hui gathered the displaced population back to the city, households slowly returned, and he began restoring the palaces until the government offices were roughly functioning again.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，關東籓表請車駕還京師。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the governors east of the pass memorialized requesting that the imperial carriage return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the governors east of the pass petitioned for the emperor's return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠之降也，義成節度使王鐸為都統，承製除官。

translations.literal: When Zhu Quanzhong surrendered, Wang Duo, military governor of Yicheng, was supreme commander and issued appointments by imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Quanzhong submitted, Wang Duo of Yicheng was supreme commander and issued appointments in the emperor's name.

sentences.zh: 全忠初鎮大梁，事鐸禮甚恭，鐸依以為援。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong first took command at Daliang, he treated Duo with great courtesy; Duo relied on him as a support.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong first took up his post at Daliang, he treated Duo with great deference, and Duo counted on him as an ally.

sentences.zh: 而全忠兵浸強，益驕倨，鐸知不足恃，表請還朝，徙鐸為義昌節度使。

translations.literal: But Quanzhong's forces grew ever stronger and he became increasingly arrogant; Duo knew he could not be relied on, memorialized requesting return to court, and Duo was transferred to be military governor of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: As Quanzhong's power grew, he grew ever more arrogant. Duo saw he could no longer rely on him, asked to return to court, and was transferred to Yichang as military governor.

sentences.zh: 鹿晏弘之去河中，王建、韓建、張造、晉暉、李師泰各帥其眾與之俱；

translations.literal: When Lu Yanhong left Hezhong, Wang Jian, Han Jian, Zhang Zao, Jin Hui, and Li Shitai each led their followers to go with him;
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Yanhong left Hezhong, Wang Jian, Han Jian, Zhang Zao, Jin Hui, and Li Shitai each led their men to follow him.

sentences.zh: 及據興元，以建等為巡內刺史，不遣之官。

translations.literal: when he seized Xingyuan, he made Jian and the others inspectors within the circuit but did not send them to take office.
translations.idiomatic: After he seized Xingyuan, he named Jian and the others as internal inspectors but never sent them to their posts.

sentences.zh: 晏弘猜忌，眾心不附，王建、韓建素相親善，晏弘尤忌之，數引入臥內，待之加厚。

translations.literal: Yanhong was suspicious by nature and the hearts of the men were not with him; Wang Jian and Han Jian had long been close, and Yanhong especially feared them, repeatedly summoning them into his private quarters and treating them with extra favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhong was suspicious and his men were not loyal. Wang Jian and Han Jian had long been close friends, and Yanhong especially distrusted them, repeatedly calling them into his private quarters and treating them with unusual warmth.

sentences.zh: 二建密相謂曰：「僕射甘言厚意，疑我也，禍將至矣！

translations.literal: The two Jians secretly said to each other: "The Vice Director's sweet words and generous treatment mean he suspects us—disaster is coming!
translations.idiomatic: The two Jians whispered to each other: "His kind words and favors mean he suspects us. Disaster is near!

sentences.zh: 」田令孜密遣人以厚利誘之，十一月，二建與張造、晉暉、李師泰帥眾數千逃奔行在，令孜皆養為假子，賜與巨萬，拜諸衛將軍，使各將其眾，號隨駕五都。

translations.literal: " Tian Lingzi secretly sent men to entice them with great profit. In the eleventh month, the two Jians with Zhang Zao, Jin Hui, and Li Shitai led several thousand men in flight to the imperial court; Lingzi adopted them all as foster sons, bestowed vast sums, appointed them generals of the guard regiments, and had each lead his followers—they were called the Five Commands of the Imperial Escort.
translations.idiomatic: " Tian Lingzi secretly sent agents to lure them with rich rewards. In the eleventh month, the two Jians fled to the emperor's camp with Zhang Zao, Jin Hui, and Li Shitai and several thousand men. Lingzi adopted them all as foster sons, gave them enormous gifts, made them generals of the guard regiments, and let each keep his own troops. They were called the Five Commands of the Imperial Escort.

sentences.zh: 又遣禁兵討晏弘，晏弘率眾棄興元走。

translations.literal: He also sent imperial guards to attack Yanhong; Yanhong led his followers in abandoning Xingyuan and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi also sent imperial guards against Yanhong, who abandoned Xingyuan and fled with his army.

sentences.zh: 初，宦者曹知愨，本華原富家子，有膽略。

translations.literal: Earlier, the eunuch Cao Zhihui was originally the son of a wealthy family in Huayuan and had courage and resourcefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the eunuch Cao Zhihui had been the son of a wealthy family in Huayuan and was bold and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 黃巢陷長安，知愨歸鄉里，集壯士，據嵯峨山南，為堡自固，巢黨不敢近。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao took Chang'an, Zhihui returned to his home district, gathered stalwarts, and held the south of Mount Cuoe, fortifying himself in a stronghold; Chao's partisans did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao seized Chang'an, Zhihui went home, gathered fighting men, and fortified himself on the south slope of Mount Cuoe. Chao's followers did not dare come near.

sentences.zh: 知愨數遣壯士變衣服語言，效巢黨，夜入長安攻賊營，賊驚以為鬼神；

translations.literal: Zhihui repeatedly sent stalwarts who changed clothes and speech to imitate Chao's partisans, entered Chang'an by night to attack rebel camps, and the rebels were alarmed, thinking it spirits;
translations.idiomatic: Zhihui repeatedly sent men disguised as Chao's followers into Chang'an by night to strike rebel camps. The rebels were terrified, thinking spirits were at work.

sentences.zh: 又疑其下有叛者，由是心不自安。

translations.literal: they also suspected traitors among themselves, and thus their hearts were not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: They also suspected traitors in their own ranks, and their morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞而嘉之，就除內常侍，賜金紫。

translations.literal: The court heard and commended him, appointing him on the spot as Palace Attendant and bestowing the gold-and-purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: The court heard of this and praised him, appointing him Palace Attendant on the spot and bestowing the gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 知愨聞車駕將還，謂人曰：「吾施小術，使諸軍得成大功，從駕群臣但平步往來，俟至大散關，當閱其可歸者納之。

translations.literal: Zhihui heard that the imperial carriage was about to return and said to people: "I used a small stratagem so the armies could achieve great merit; the ministers accompanying the carriage merely walk back and forth at ease—when we reach Dasan Pass, I shall review who may return and admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the emperor was about to return, Zhihui said: "I used a small trick so the armies could win great glory, while the courtiers who followed the throne simply strolled back and forth. When we reach Dasan Pass, I will sort out who deserves to go home and who does not.

sentences.zh: 」行在聞之，恐其為變；

translations.literal: " The imperial court heard this and feared he would make trouble;
translations.idiomatic: " The court heard this and feared he would stir up trouble.

sentences.zh: 田令孜尤惡之，密以敕旨諭邠寧節度使王行瑜，使誅之。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi especially hated him and secretly conveyed imperial orders to Wang Xingyu, military governor of Binning, to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi especially hated him and secretly ordered Wang Xingyu, military governor of Binning, to kill him.

sentences.zh: 行瑜潛師自嵯峨山北乘高攻之，知愨不為備，舉營盡殪。

translations.literal: Xingyu sent troops secretly from north of Mount Cuoe to attack from the heights; Zhihui was unprepared, and his entire camp was annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu sent troops secretly from north of Mount Cuoe to attack from above. Zhihui was unprepared, and his entire camp was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 令孜益驕橫，禁制天子，不得有所主斷。

translations.literal: Lingzi grew ever more arrogant and overbearing, restraining the Son of Heaven so that he could make no decisions of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi grew ever more arrogant and domineering, keeping the emperor from making any decision on his own.

sentences.zh: 上患其專，時語左右而流涕。

translations.literal: The emperor resented his monopoly of power and at times spoke to those beside him with tears.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resented his grip on power and sometimes wept as he spoke to those around him.

sentences.zh: 鹿晏弘引兵東出襄州，秦宗權遣其將秦誥、趙德諲將兵會之，共攻襄州，陷之；

translations.literal: Lu Yanhong led his troops east out of Xiangzhou; Qin Zongquan sent his generals Qin Hao and Zhao Deneng with troops to join him, and together they attacked Xiangzhou and took it;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanhong marched east from Xiangzhou. Qin Zongquan sent Qin Hao and Zhao Deneng with troops to join him, and together they captured Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使劉臣容奔成都。

translations.literal: Liu Chenrong, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, fled to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chenrong, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, fled to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 德諲，蔡州人也。

translations.literal: Deneng was a man of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deneng was a native of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 晏弘引兵轉掠襄、鄧、均、房、廬、壽，復還許州。

translations.literal: Yanhong led his troops in turn to raid Xiang, Deng, Jun, Fang, Lu, and Shou, then returned again to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhong marched on, plundering Xiang, Deng, Jun, Fang, Lu, and Shou, then returned to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 忠武節度使周岌聞其至，棄鎮走，晏弘遂據許州，自稱留後，朝廷不能討，因以為忠武節度使。

translations.literal: Zhou Ji, military governor of Zhongwu, heard he had arrived, abandoned his post and fled; Yanhong then seized Xuzhou, styled himself acting military governor, and the court could not punish him, so he was appointed military governor of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ji of Zhongwu fled his post when he heard Yanhong was coming. Yanhong seized Xuzhou, declared himself acting governor, and because the court could not subdue him, was recognized as military governor of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己丑，陳敬瑄表辭三川都指揮、招討、制置、安撫等使，從之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jichou day, Chen Jingxuan memorialized resigning the posts of supreme commander, campaign commander, commissioner for regulation, and pacification commissioner of the Three Circuits of Sichuan; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jichou day, Chen Jingxuan asked to resign as supreme commander, campaign commander, and pacification commissioner of the Three Circuits of Sichuan. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，黃巢轉掠福建，建州人陳巖聚眾數千保鄉里，號九龍軍，福建觀察使鄭鎰奏為團練副使。

translations.literal: Earlier, Huang Chao swept through Fujian; Chen Yan of Jianzhou gathered several thousand men to defend his home district, styled them the Nine Dragons Army, and Zheng Yi, observation commissioner of Fujian, memorialized appointing him deputy militia commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Huang Chao ravaged Fujian, Chen Yan of Jianzhou raised several thousand men to defend his home district and called them the Nine Dragons Army. Zheng Yi, observation commissioner of Fujian, recommended him as deputy militia commissioner.

sentences.zh: 泉州刺史、左廂都虞候李連有罪，亡入溪洞，合眾攻福州，巖擊敗之。

translations.literal: Li Lian, prefect of Quanzhou and chief inspector of the left wing, was guilty of a crime, fled into the mountain ravines, gathered followers to attack Fuzhou, and Yan defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lian, prefect of Quanzhou and chief inspector of the left wing, had committed a crime and fled into the hill country. He gathered a force and attacked Fuzhou, but Yan defeated him.

sentences.zh: 鎰畏巖之逼，表巖自代，壬寅，以巖為福建觀察使。

translations.literal: Yi feared Yan's pressure, memorialized that Yan replace him, and on renyin day Yan was made observation commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, fearing Yan's power, asked that Yan replace him. On renyin day, Yan was appointed observation commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 巖為治有威惠，閩人安之。

translations.literal: Yan's governance combined authority and kindness, and the people of Min were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yan governed with both firmness and kindness, and the people of Min lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 義昌節度使兼中書令王鐸，厚於奉養，過魏州，侍妾成列，服御鮮華，如承平之態。

translations.literal: Wang Duo, military governor of Yichang and concurrently Director of the Chancellery, was lavish in his maintenance; passing through Weizhou, his concubines formed a long line and his equipage was fresh and splendid, as in times of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo, military governor of Yichang and concurrently Director of the Chancellery, lived in great luxury. Passing through Weizhou, his concubines marched in a long procession and his equipage was bright and splendid, as if the empire were still at peace.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使樂彥禎之子從訓，伏卒數百人於漳南高雞泊，圍而殺之，及賓僚從者三百餘人皆死，掠其資裝侍妾而還。

translations.literal: Le Congxun, son of Le Yanzhen, military governor of Weibo, hid several hundred soldiers at Gaojipo south of Zhang, surrounded and killed him, and more than three hundred guests, officials, and attendants all died; they plundered his goods, equipage, and concubines and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Le Congxun, son of Le Yanzhen of Weibo, ambushed him with several hundred men at Gaojipo south of Zhang. Duo and more than three hundred guests, officials, and attendants were killed. They stripped his goods and concubines and went home.

sentences.zh: 彥禎奏雲為盜所殺，朝廷不能詰。

translations.literal: Yanzhen memorialized that clouds had killed him as bandits would; the court could not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen reported that bandits had killed him. The court could not press the matter.

sentences.zh: 賜邠寧軍號曰靜難。

translations.literal: The Binning Army was granted the designation Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The Binning Army was given the designation Jingnan, "Pacifying Difficulties."

sentences.zh: 是歲，餘杭鎮使陳晟逐睦州刺史柳超，穎州都知兵馬使汝陰王敬蕘逐其刺史，各領州事，朝廷因命為刺史。

translations.literal: That year, Chen Sheng, garrison commissioner of Yuhang, drove out Liu Chao, prefect of Muzhou; Wang Jingyao of Ruyin, chief military commissioner of Yingzhou, drove out its prefect; each took charge of his prefecture, and the court accordingly appointed them prefects.
translations.idiomatic: That year Chen Sheng of Yuhang drove out the prefect of Muzhou, and Wang Jingyao of Yingzhou drove out its prefect. Each seized control of his prefecture, and the court duly recognized them as prefects.

sentences.zh: 均州賊帥孫喜聚眾數千人，謀攻州城，刺史呂燁不知所為。

translations.literal: Sun Xi, bandit chief of Junzhou, gathered several thousand men and plotted to attack the prefectural city; the prefect Lü Ye did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xi, a rebel leader in Junzhou, raised several thousand men and planned to storm the prefectural city. Prefect Lü Ye was at a loss.

sentences.zh: 都將武當馮行襲伏兵江南，自乘小舟迎喜，謂曰：「州人得良牧，無不歸心，然公所從之卒大多，州人懼於剽掠，尚以為疑。

translations.literal: Feng Xingsi of Wudang, a garrison commander, hid troops south of the river, himself took a small boat to meet Xi, and said: "The people of the prefecture, having gained a good governor, all give him their hearts; yet the soldiers following you, sir, are too many, and the people fear plunder and still harbor doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xingsi of Wudang, a garrison commander, hid troops south of the river and rowed out in a small boat to meet Xi. He said: "The people are glad to have a good governor and would welcome you, but your followers are too many. The townspeople fear looting and are still uneasy.

sentences.zh: 不若置軍江北，獨與腹心輕騎俱進，行襲請為前道，告諭州人，無不服者矣。

translations.literal: Would it not be better to leave the army north of the river and advance with trusted men and light cavalry alone? Xingsi asks to go ahead on the road, proclaiming to the people of the prefecture—none will fail to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Why not leave your army north of the river and come in with only your closest men and a light escort? Let me go ahead and announce your arrival. No one will refuse to submit.

sentences.zh: 」喜以為然，從之；

translations.literal: " Xi thought this right and followed it;
translations.idiomatic: " Xi agreed and did as he suggested.

sentences.zh: 既渡江，軍吏迎謁，伏兵發，行襲手擊喜，斬之，從喜者皆死，江北軍望之俱潰。

translations.literal: once they had crossed the river, officers came out to welcome them, the ambush sprang, Xingsi struck Xi with his own hand and beheaded him, all who followed Xi died, and the army north of the river, seeing this, all collapsed in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had crossed the river, officials came out to greet them and the ambush sprang. Xingsi struck Xi down with his own hand and cut off his head. All who had come with Xi were killed, and the army north of the river broke and fled at the sight.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使上其功，詔以行襲為均州刺史。

translations.literal: The military governor of Shannan East Circuit reported his merit, and an edict appointed Xingsi prefect of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The military governor of Shannan East Circuit reported his exploit, and the court appointed Xingsi prefect of Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 州西有長山，當襄、鄧入蜀之道，群盜據之，抄掠貢賦，行襲討誅之，蜀道以通。

translations.literal: West of the prefecture was Mount Chang, on the road from Xiang and Deng into Shu; bandits held it and plundered tribute and taxes; Xingsi attacked and executed them, and the road into Shu was opened.
translations.idiomatic: West of the prefecture stood Mount Chang, on the road from Xiang and Deng into Shu. Bandits held it and robbed tribute convoys. Xingsi attacked and destroyed them, and the road into Shu was open again.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔節度使李昌言病，表弟昌符知留後。

translations.literal: Li Changyan, military governor of Fengxiang, fell ill; his younger cousin Changfu acted as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changyan, military governor of Fengxiang, fell ill, and his younger cousin Changfu took charge as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 昌言薨，制以昌符為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: Changyan died; by imperial order Changfu was made military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Changyan died, the court appointed Changfu military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 時黃巢雖平，秦宗權復熾，命將出兵，寇掠鄰道，陳彥侵淮南，秦賢侵江南，秦誥陷襄、唐、鄧，孫儒陷東都、孟、陝、虢，張晊陷汝、鄭，盧瑭攻汴、宋，所至屠翦焚蕩，殆無孑遺。

translations.literal: At that time, although Huang Chao was pacified, Qin Zongquan flourished again; he ordered his generals to lead troops out and raid neighboring circuits—Chen Yan invaded Huainan, Qin Xian invaded Jiangnan, Qin Hao took Xiang, Tang, and Deng, Sun Ru took the eastern capital, Meng, Shaan, and Guo, Zhang Zhi took Ru and Zheng, Lu Tang attacked Bian and Song; wherever they went they slaughtered, cut down, burned, and swept clean, until scarcely a soul remained.
translations.idiomatic: Although Huang Chao had been crushed, Qin Zongquan rose again. He sent his generals to ravage neighboring circuits: Chen Yan into Huainan, Qin Xian into Jiangnan, Qin Hao into Xiang, Tang, and Deng, Sun Ru into the eastern capital, Meng, Shaan, and Guo, Zhang Zhi into Ru and Zheng, Lu Tang against Bian and Song. Wherever they marched they slaughtered and burned until scarcely anyone was left alive.

sentences.zh: 其殘暴又甚於巢，軍行未始轉糧，車載鹽屍以從。

translations.literal: Their cruelty exceeded even Chao's; the army never transported grain on the march but loaded carts with salted corpses to follow along.
translations.idiomatic: They were even more brutal than Chao's men. The army never carried grain on campaign but loaded carts with salted human flesh instead.

sentences.zh: 北至衛、滑，西及關輔，東盡青、齊，南出江、淮，州鎮存者僅保一城，極目千里，無復煙火。

translations.literal: North to Wei and Hua, west to the capital region, east to Qing and Qi, south to the Yangtze and Huai—of the prefectures and garrisons that survived, most held only a single city; for a thousand li in every direction there was no smoke or fire.
translations.idiomatic: North to Wei and Hua, west to the capital region, east to Qing and Qi, south to the Yangtze and Huai—the surviving towns held at most a single walled city. For a thousand li in every direction, not a wisp of hearth smoke remained.

sentences.zh: 上將還長安、畏宗權為患。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to return to Chang'an but feared Zongquan as a peril.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to return to Chang'an but feared what Zongquan might do.

sentences.zh: 僖宗惠聖恭定孝皇帝下之上光啟元年（

translations.literal: Below [the account of] Emperor Xizong Huisheng Gongding Xiaoxiao, Part One: Guangqi year 1 (
translations.idiomatic: Below [the account of] Emperor Xizong, Huisheng Gongding Xiaoxiao, Part One—Guangqi year 1 (

sentences.zh: 乙巳，公元八八五年）

translations.literal: Yisi, equivalent to 885 CE)
translations.idiomatic: Yisi, equivalent to 885 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊午，下詔招撫之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on wuwu day, an edict was issued to offer amnesty and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on wuwu day, the court issued an edict offering amnesty and reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 己卯，車駕發成都，陳敬瑄送至漢州而還。

translations.literal: On jimao day the imperial carriage set out from Chengdu; Chen Jingxuan escorted it to Hanzhou and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day the imperial procession left Chengdu. Chen Jingxuan escorted it as far as Hanzhou and then turned back.

sentences.zh: 荊南監軍朱敬玫所募忠勇軍暴橫，節度使陳儒患之。

translations.literal: The Loyal and Brave Army recruited by Zhu Jingmei, military supervisor of Jingnan, was violent and overbearing; the military governor Chen Ru was troubled by them.
translations.idiomatic: The Loyal and Brave Army raised by Zhu Jingmei, the military supervisor of Jingnan, ran riot, and Military Governor Chen Ru was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 鄭紹業之鎮荊南也，遣大將申屠琮將兵五千擊黃巢於長安。

translations.literal: When Zheng Shaoye took command of Jingnan, he sent the great general Shentu Cong with five thousand troops to attack Huang Chao at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Shaoye was posted to Jingnan, he had sent the general Shentu Cong with five thousand men to fight Huang Chao at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 軍還，儒告琮，使除之。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Ru told Cong and had him eliminate them.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops came back, Ru enlisted Cong to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 忠勇將程君之聞之，帥其眾奔朗州，琮追擊之，殺百餘人，餘眾皆潰，自是琮復專軍政。

translations.literal: The Loyal and Brave officer Cheng Junzhi heard of this, led his followers to flee to Langzhou; Cong pursued and attacked, killed more than a hundred, and the rest all scattered. From then on Cong again monopolized military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Junzhi, an officer of the Loyal and Brave Army, heard of the plan and led his men to Langzhou. Cong pursued them, killed over a hundred, and the rest fled. From that point Cong once again held sole control of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 雷滿屢攻掠荊南，儒重賂以卻之。

translations.literal: Lei Man repeatedly attacked and plundered Jingnan; Ru heavily bribed him to drive him off.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Man raided Jingnan again and again; Ru bought him off with heavy bribes.

sentences.zh: 淮南將張瑰、韓師德叛高駢，據復、岳二州，自稱刺史，儒請瑰攝行軍司馬，師德攝節度副使，將兵擊雷滿。

translations.literal: The Huainan generals Zhang Gui and Han Shide rebelled against Gao Pian, seized the two prefectures of Fu and Yue, and styled themselves prefects. Ru asked that Gui act as acting campaign secretary and Shide as acting deputy military governor, and led troops to attack Lei Man.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan generals Zhang Gui and Han Shide rebelled against Gao Pian, seized Fu and Yue, and declared themselves prefects. Ru appointed Gui acting campaign secretary and Shide acting deputy military governor, then marched against Lei Man.

sentences.zh: 師德引兵上峽大掠，歸於岳州，瑰還兵逐儒而代之。

translations.literal: Shide led troops up the gorges and plundered on a great scale, then returned to Yuezhou. Gui turned his army back, drove Ru out, and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Shide led his men through the gorges and looted heavily before returning to Yuezhou. Gui then turned his army around, expelled Ru, and took his place.

sentences.zh: 儒將奔行在，瑰劫還，囚之。

translations.literal: Ru was about to flee to the imperial court; Gui intercepted him on the road, brought him back, and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Ru tried to flee to the emperor's camp, but Gui intercepted him, brought him back, and threw him in prison.

sentences.zh: 瑰，渭州人，性貪暴，荊南舊將夷滅殆盡。

translations.literal: Gui was a man of Weizhou, greedy and brutal by nature; he nearly exterminated all the old generals of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was from Weizhou, greedy and savage by nature, and he nearly wiped out every veteran general in Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 先是，朱敬玫屢殺大將及富商以致富，朝廷遣中使楊玄晦代之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhu Jingmei had repeatedly killed great generals and wealthy merchants to enrich himself; the court sent the palace emissary Yang Xuanhui to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhu Jingmei had grown rich by repeatedly killing senior generals and wealthy merchants. The court sent the palace envoy Yang Xuanhui to replace him.

sentences.zh: 敬玫留居荊南，嘗曝衣。

translations.literal: Jingmei remained in Jingnan and once aired out his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmei stayed on in Jingnan and once hung his clothes out to dry.

sentences.zh: 瑰見而欲之，遣卒夜攻之，殺敬玫，盡取其財。

translations.literal: Gui saw them and coveted them; he sent soldiers to attack by night, killed Jingmei, and took all his wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Gui saw the display and coveted it. He sent men to attack at night, killed Jingmei, and seized all his property.

sentences.zh: 瑰惡牙將郭禹慓悍，欲殺之，禹結黨千人亡去，庚申，襲歸州，據之，自稱刺史。

translations.literal: Gui hated the staff general Guo Yu for his fierce boldness and wished to kill him. Yu gathered a faction of a thousand men and fled. On gengshen day he raided Guizhou, seized it, and styled himself prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Gui hated the staff general Guo Yu for his fierce, unruly spirit and wanted him dead. Yu rallied a thousand followers and fled. On gengshen day he seized Guizhou, held it, and declared himself prefect.

sentences.zh: 禹，青州人成汭也，因殺人亡命，更其姓名。

translations.literal: Yu was Cheng Wei of Qingzhou; because he had killed a man and fled for his life, he changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was really Cheng Wei of Qingzhou, a fugitive who had killed a man and taken a new name.

sentences.zh: 南康賊帥盧光稠陷虔州，自稱刺史，以其裡人譚全播為謀主。

translations.literal: The Nankang bandit chief Lu Guangchou captured Qianzhou, styled himself prefect, and made his fellow townsman Tan Quanbo his chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: The Nankang bandit leader Lu Guangchou took Qianzhou, declared himself prefect, and made his townsman Tan Quanbo his chief adviser.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權責租賦於光州刺史王緒，緒不能給，宗權怒，發兵擊之。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan demanded rent and taxes from Wang Xu, prefect of Guangzhou; Xu could not supply them. Zongquan grew angry and sent troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan demanded taxes from Wang Xu, the prefect of Guangzhou. When Xu could not pay, Zongquan flew into a rage and sent troops against him.

sentences.zh: 緒懼，悉舉光、壽兵五千人，驅吏民渡江，以劉行全為前鋒，轉掠江、洪、虔州，是月，陷汀、漳二州，然皆不能守也。

translations.literal: Xu was afraid; he mustered all five thousand troops of Guang and Shou, drove officials and commoners across the river, made Liu Xingquan vanguard, and turned to plunder Jiang, Hong, and Qian prefectures. That month he captured Ting and Zhang, but could hold neither.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Xu gathered all five thousand troops from Guang and Shou, forced officials and civilians across the Yangzi, and put Liu Xingquan in the vanguard. They swept through Jiang, Hong, and Qian, and that month took Ting and Zhang—but could hold neither.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權寇穎、亳，朱全忠敗之於焦夷。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan raided Ying and Bo; Zhu Quanzhong defeated him at Jiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan invaded Ying and Bo; Zhu Quanzhong defeated him at Jiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙申，車駕至鳳翔。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingshen day, the imperial carriage reached Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingshen day, the emperor reached Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁卯，至京師；

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingmao day, he reached the capital;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingmao day, he reached the capital;

sentences.zh: 荊棘滿城，狐兔縱橫，上淒然不樂。

translations.literal: thorns filled the city, foxes and hares ran everywhere, and the emperor was desolate and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: thorns choked the streets, foxes and hares ran wild through the ruins, and the emperor was stricken with grief.

sentences.zh: 己巳，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On jisi day he granted a general amnesty and changed the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day he proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign era.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷號令所在，惟河西、山南、劍南、嶺南數十州而已。

translations.literal: At that time the court's orders reached only several dozen prefectures in Hexi, Shannan, Jiannan, and Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: By then the court's authority extended to only a few dozen prefectures in Hexi, Shannan, Jiannan, and Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權稱帝，置百官，詔以武寧節度使時溥為蔡州四面行營兵馬都統以討之。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan declared himself emperor, established the full bureaucracy, and an edict appointed Shi Pu, military governor of Wuning, supreme commander of the encircling campaign forces around Caizhou to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan declared himself emperor and set up a full court. The throne appointed Shi Pu, military governor of Wuning, supreme commander of the encircling forces at Caizhou to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 盧龍節度使李可舉、成德節度使王鎔惡李克用之強，而義武節度使王處存與克用親善，為侄鄴娶克用女。

translations.literal: Li Keju, military governor of Lulong, and Wang Rong, military governor of Chengde, hated Li Keyong's strength, while Wang Chucun, military governor of Yiwu, was on close terms with Keyong and had his nephew Ye marry Keyong's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keju of Lulong and Wang Rong of Chengde resented Li Keyong's power, but Wang Chucun of Yiwu was on friendly terms with Keyong and had his nephew Ye marry Keyong's daughter.

sentences.zh: 又，河北諸鎮，惟義武尚屬朝廷，可舉等恐其窺伺山東，終為己患，乃相與謀曰：「易、定，燕、趙之餘也。

translations.literal: Moreover, among the Hebei garrisons only Yiwu still belonged to the court. Keju and the others feared that it would watch for a chance in Shandong and in the end become a threat to them, so they plotted together, saying: "Yi and Ding are what remain of Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Hebei garrisons, only Yiwu still answered to the court. Keju and the others feared that Chucun would eye Shandong and eventually become their enemy, so they plotted together: "Yi and Ding are all that remain of Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 」約共滅處存而分其地。

translations.literal: " They agreed jointly to destroy Chucun and divide his territory.
translations.idiomatic: " They agreed to destroy Chucun together and divide his land.

sentences.zh: 又說雲中節度使赫連鐸使攻克用之背。

translations.literal: They also persuaded Helian Duo, military governor of Yunzhong, to strike Keyong from behind.
translations.idiomatic: They also persuaded Helian Duo, military governor of Yunzhong, to attack Keyong from the rear.

sentences.zh: 可舉遣其將李全忠將兵六萬攻易州，鎔遣將將兵攻無極。

translations.literal: Keju sent his general Li Quanzhong with sixty thousand troops to attack Yizhou; Rong sent a general with troops to attack Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: Keju sent his general Li Quanzhong with sixty thousand men against Yizhou, while Rong sent a general to attack Wuji.

sentences.zh: 處存告急於克用，克用遣其將康君立等將兵救之。

translations.literal: Chucun reported the emergency to Keyong; Keyong sent his generals Kang Junli and others with troops to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Chucun appealed to Keyong for help, and Keyong sent Kang Junli and other generals to his relief.

sentences.zh: 閏月，秦宗權遣其弟宗言寇荊南。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Qin Zongquan sent his younger brother Zongyan to raid Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Qin Zongquan sent his brother Zongyan to invade Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 初，田令孜在蜀募新軍五十四都，每都千人，分隸兩神策，為十軍以統之，又南牙、北司官共萬餘員。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tian Lingzi in Shu had recruited a new army of fifty-four companies, a thousand men in each, assigned them to the two Shence Armies, and organized them into ten corps to command them; officials of the Southern Bureau and Northern Bureau together numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while in Shu, Tian Lingzi had raised a new army of fifty-four companies of a thousand men each, assigned them to the two Shence Armies under ten corps, and expanded the Southern and Northern Bureaus to more than ten thousand officials.

sentences.zh: 是時籓鎮各專租稅，河南、北、江、淮無復上供，三司轉運無調發之所，度支惟收京畿、同、華、鳳翔等數州租稅，不能贍，賞賚不時，士卒有怨言。

translations.literal: At that time each garrison monopolized its own rents and taxes; Henan, Hebei, the Yangzi, and the Huai no longer sent tribute upward. The Three Offices of Transport had nowhere from which to requisition supplies. The Department of Revenue could collect rents and taxes only from the capital region, Tong, Hua, Fengxiang, and a few other prefectures, and could not meet expenses. Rewards and gifts were not issued on time, and the soldiers murmured in complaint.
translations.idiomatic: By then each garrison kept its own taxes; Henan, Hebei, the Yangzi, and the Huai sent nothing to the capital. The transport offices had nowhere to draw supplies. Revenue came only from the capital region, Tong, Hua, Fengxiang, and a handful of other prefectures—not enough to pay the bills. Rewards came late, and the soldiers grumbled.

sentences.zh: 令孜患之，不知所出。

translations.literal: Lingzi was troubled by this and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi was alarmed and could see no way out.

sentences.zh: 先是，安邑、解縣兩池鹽皆隸鹽鐵，置官榷之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the two salt ponds of Anyi and Jie county had both belonged to the Salt and Iron Commission, with officials appointed to monopolize them.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the salt ponds at Anyi and Jie county had belonged to the Salt and Iron Commission and were run as a state monopoly.

sentences.zh: 中和以來，河中節度使王重榮專之，歲獻三千車以供國用，令孜奏復如舊制隸鹽鐵。

translations.literal: Since the Zhonghe era, Wang Chongrong, military governor of Hezhong, had monopolized them and each year presented three thousand cartloads for state use. Lingzi memorialized that they should again, as under the old system, be placed under the Salt and Iron Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhonghe era, Wang Chongrong of Hezhong had controlled them, sending three thousand cartloads of salt each year for the state. Lingzi petitioned to restore the old system and put them back under the Salt and Iron Commission.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，令孜自兼兩池榷鹽使，收其利以贍軍。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Lingzi personally added to his titles the post of salt monopoly commissioner for the two ponds, taking their profits to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Lingzi made himself commissioner of the two salt ponds, seizing their profits to pay the troops.

sentences.zh: 重榮上章論訴不已，遣中使往諭之，重榮不可。

translations.literal: Chongrong submitted memorial after memorial arguing and protesting without cease. The court sent a palace emissary to instruct him, but Chongrong would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong kept sending memorials of protest. The court dispatched a palace envoy to reason with him, but Chongrong refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 時令孜多遣親信覘籓鎮，有不附己者，輒圖之。

translations.literal: At that time Lingzi often sent trusted intimates to spy on the garrisons; whenever any did not support him, he would plot against them.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi constantly sent trusted agents to watch the garrisons, and whenever one failed to support him, he plotted its downfall.

sentences.zh: 令孜養子匡祐使河中，重榮待之甚厚，而匡祐傲甚，舉軍皆憤怒。

translations.literal: Lingzi's adopted son Kuang You was sent on a mission to Hezhong. Chongrong treated him very generously, yet Kuang You was extremely arrogant, and the whole army grew furious.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi's adopted son Kuang You was sent to Hezhong. Chongrong treated him lavishly, but Kuang You was insufferably arrogant, and the entire army seethed with anger.

sentences.zh: 重榮乃數令敢罪惡，責其無禮，監軍為講解，僅得脫去。

translations.literal: Chongrong then repeatedly listed Lingzi's crimes and rebuked Kuang You for his lack of courtesy. The army supervisor mediated, and Kuang You barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong then listed Lingzi's crimes one by one and rebuked Kuang You for his insolence. The army supervisor intervened, and Kuang You barely got away alive.

sentences.zh: 匡祐歸，以告令孜，勸圖之。

translations.literal: Kuang You returned and told Lingzi, urging him to plot against Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang You returned, reported everything to Lingzi, and urged him to destroy Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 五月，令孜徙重榮為泰寧節度使，以泰寧節度使齊克讓為義武節度使，以義武節度使王處存為河中節度使，仍詔李克用以河東軍援處存赴鎮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Lingzi transferred Chongrong to be military governor of Taining, made Qi Kerang, military governor of Taining, military governor of Yiwu, and Wang Chucun, military governor of Yiwu, military governor of Hezhong, and also ordered Li Keyong to support Chucun with Hedong troops as he went to take up his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Lingzi transferred Chongrong to Taining, moved Qi Kerang from Taining to Yiwu, and posted Wang Chucun from Yiwu to Hezhong. He also ordered Li Keyong to escort Chucun to his new command with Hedong troops.

sentences.zh: 盧龍兵攻易州，裨將劉仁恭穴地入城，遂克之。

translations.literal: The Lulong army attacked Yizhou; the subordinate general Liu Rengong tunneled into the city and thus captured it.
translations.idiomatic: The Lulong army besieged Yizhou; the subordinate general Liu Rengong tunneled into the city and took it.

sentences.zh: 仁恭，深州人也。

translations.literal: Rengong was a man of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong was from Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 李克用自將救無極，敗成德兵。

translations.literal: Li Keyong personally led troops to rescue Wuji and defeated the Chengde army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong personally led a relief force to Wuji and routed the Chengde army.

sentences.zh: 成德兵退保新城，克用復進擊，大破之，拔新城，成德兵走，追至九門，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: The Chengde army withdrew to hold Xincheng. Keyong pressed the attack again, routed them thoroughly, took Xincheng, and the Chengde army fled. He pursued to Jiumen and cut off more than ten thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengde army fell back to Xincheng. Keyong attacked again, smashed them, and took the city. He pursued the fleeing Chengde troops to Jiumen and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 盧龍兵既得易州，驕怠，王處存夜遣卒三千蒙羊皮造城下，盧龍兵以為羊也，爭出掠之，處存奮擊，大破之，復取易州，李全忠走。

translations.literal: Once the Lulong army had taken Yizhou, it grew arrogant and slack. Wang Chucun by night sent three thousand soldiers covered in sheepskins to approach the walls. The Lulong army thought they were sheep and rushed out to seize them. Chucun struck hard, routed them thoroughly, retook Yizhou, and Li Quanzhong fled.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Yizhou, the Lulong army grew arrogant and careless. Chucun sent three thousand men covered in sheepskins to the walls by night. The Lulong troops took them for sheep and rushed out to catch them. Chucun attacked fiercely, routed them, retook Yizhou, and Li Quanzhong fled.

sentences.zh: 加陝虢節度使王重盈同平章事。

translations.literal: Wang Chongying, military governor of Shan-Guo, was promoted to honorary chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongying, military governor of Shan-Guo, was made honorary chief minister.

sentences.zh: 李全忠既喪師，恐獲罪，收餘眾還襲幽州。

translations.literal: Li Quanzhong, having lost his army, feared punishment; he gathered the remaining troops and returned to raid Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost his army, Li Quanzhong feared punishment and turned back with his survivors to strike at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，李可舉窘急，舉族登樓自焚死，全忠自為留後。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Li Keju, in desperate straits, led his whole clan up a tower and burned themselves to death. Quanzhong made himself acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Li Keju, cornered and desperate, led his entire family up a tower and burned themselves to death. Quanzhong declared himself acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 東都留守李罕之與秦宗權將孫儒相拒數月，罕之兵少食盡，棄城，西保澠池，宗權陷東都。

translations.literal: Li Hanzhi, defender of the Eastern Capital, and Sun Ru, general of Qin Zongquan, faced each other for several months. Hanzhi's troops were few and food ran out; he abandoned the city, withdrew west to hold Mianchi, and Zongquan captured the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhi, defender of Luoyang, and Sun Ru, a general of Qin Zongquan, fought for months. Hanzhi's men were few and supplies ran out. He abandoned the city, withdrew west to Mianchi, and Zongquan took Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以李全忠為盧龍留後。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Li Quanzhong was appointed acting military governor of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Li Quanzhong was confirmed as acting military governor of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，右補闕常浚上疏，以為：「陛下姑息籓鎮太甚，是非功過，駢首並足，致天下紛紛若此，猶未之寤，豈可不念駱谷之艱危，復懷西顧之計乎！

translations.literal: On yisi day, Right Remonstrance Official Chang Jun submitted a memorial, stating: "Your Majesty indulges the garrisons too far; right and wrong, merit and fault, are treated indiscriminately alike, bringing the realm to such turmoil—and still you have not awakened to it. How can you fail to remember the peril at Luogu Pass and again harbor plans to look westward!
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day, Right Remonstrance Official Chang Jun submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty indulges the garrisons far too much—merit and fault, right and wrong, all treated alike—and has brought the realm to this chaos. Yet you still do not see it. Have you forgotten the peril at Luogu Pass? Will you again turn your eyes westward and flee?

sentences.zh: 宜稍振典刑以威四方。

translations.literal: You should somewhat revive law and punishment to awe the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: You should restore the authority of law to awe the realm.

sentences.zh: 」田令孜之黨言於上曰：「此疏傳於籓鎮，豈不致其猜忿！

translations.literal: " Tian Lingzi's faction said to the emperor: "If this memorial spreads among the garrisons, will it not provoke their suspicion and anger!
translations.idiomatic: " Tian Lingzi's faction told the emperor: "If this memorial reaches the garrisons, it will only stir their suspicion and rage!

sentences.zh: 」庚戌，貶浚萬州司戶，尋賜死。

translations.literal: " On gengxu day Jun was demoted to registrar of Wanzhou; soon afterward he was ordered to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: " On gengxu day Jun was demoted to registrar of Wanzhou, and soon after was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 滄州軍亂，逐節度使楊全玫，立牙將盧彥威為留後，全玫奔幽州。

translations.literal: The Cangzhou army mutinied, drove out Military Governor Yang Quanmei, and installed the staff general Lu Yanwei as acting military governor. Quanmei fled to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Cangzhou garrison mutinied, expelled Military Governor Yang Quanmei, and made the staff general Lu Yanwei acting governor. Quanmei fled to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 以保鑾都將曹誠為義昌節度使，以彥威為德州刺史。

translations.literal: Cao Cheng, commander of the Imperial Guard detachment, was appointed military governor of Yichang, and Yanwei was made prefect of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cheng, a commander of the Imperial Guard, was appointed military governor of Yichang, and Yanwei was made prefect of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 孫儒據東都月餘，燒宮室、官寺、民居，大掠席捲而去，城中寂無雞犬。

translations.literal: Sun Ru held the Eastern Capital for more than a month, burned palaces, government temples, and private dwellings, plundered on a sweeping scale, and departed; the city was silent, without even a chicken or dog.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru held Luoyang for more than a month, burned palaces, temples, and homes, looted everything he could carry, and left. The city fell silent—not a chicken or dog remained.

sentences.zh: 李罕之復引其眾入東都，築壘於市西而居之。

translations.literal: Li Hanzhi again led his followers into the Eastern Capital, built fortifications west of the market, and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhi marched back into Luoyang with his men, built a fortified camp west of the market, and made it his base.

sentences.zh: 王重榮自以有復京城功，為田令孜所擯，不肯之兗州，累表論令孜離間君臣，數令孜十罪，令孜結邠寧節充使朱玫、鳳翔節度使李昌符以抗之。

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong considered that he had the merit of recovering the capital and, having been pushed aside by Tian Lingzi, refused to go to Yanzhou. He repeatedly submitted memorials arguing that Lingzi had driven ruler and ministers apart, listed ten crimes of Lingzi, and Lingzi allied with Zhu Mei, military commissioner of Binning, and Li Changfu, military governor of Fengxiang, to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong believed he deserved credit for recovering the capital. Pushed aside by Tian Lingzi, he refused to go to Yanzhou and sent memorial after memorial accusing Lingzi of driving a wedge between emperor and ministers, listing ten crimes against him. Lingzi rallied Zhu Mei of Binning and Li Changfu of Fengxiang to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 王處存亦上言：「幽、鎮兵新退，臣未敢離易、定。

translations.literal: Wang Chucun also submitted a memorial: "The You and Zhen armies have only just withdrawn; your servant dares not leave Yi and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun also wrote: "The armies from You and Zhen have only just withdrawn; I dare not leave Yi and Ding.

sentences.zh: 且王重榮無罪，有大功於國，不宜輕有改易，搖籓鎮心。

translations.literal: Moreover, Wang Chongrong is without guilt and has great merit to the state; he should not lightly be transferred, shaking the hearts of the garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Wang Chongrong is innocent and has served the state well. He should not be moved lightly, or the garrisons will lose heart.

sentences.zh: 」詔趣其上道。

translations.literal: " An edict urged him to set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne ordered him to depart at once.

sentences.zh: 八月，處存引軍至晉州，刺史冀君武閉城不內而還。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Chucun led his army to Jizhou; the prefect Ji Junwu closed the city and would not admit him, so he returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Chucun marched to Jizhou, but Prefect Ji Junwu shut the gates against him, and Chucun turned back.

sentences.zh: 洺州刺史馬爽，與昭義行軍司馬奚忠信不葉，起兵屯邢州南，脅孟方立請誅忠信。

translations.literal: Ma Shuang, prefect of Mingzhou, was at odds with Xi Zhongxin, campaign secretary of Zhaoyi; he raised troops and encamped south of Xingzhou, coercing Meng Fangli to request Zhongxin's execution.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shuang, prefect of Mingzhou, fell out with Xi Zhongxin, campaign secretary of Zhaoyi. He raised troops and camped south of Xingzhou, forcing Meng Fangli to demand Zhongxin's death.

sentences.zh: 既而眾潰，爽奔魏州，忠信使人賂樂彥禎而殺之。

translations.literal: Before long the force collapsed; Shuang fled to Weizhou, and Zhongxin sent men to bribe Yue Yanzhen and have him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the force disintegrated. Shuang fled to Weizhou, and Zhongxin bribed Yue Yanzhen to have him killed.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權攻鄰道二十餘州，陷之；

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan attacked more than twenty neighboring prefectures and captured them;
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan attacked more than twenty neighboring prefectures and took them;

sentences.zh: 唯陳州距蔡百餘里，兵力甚弱，刺史趙犨日與宗權戰，宗權不能屈。

translations.literal: only Chenzhou, little more than a hundred li from Cai, had very weak forces, yet its prefect Zhao Chou fought Zongquan day after day, and Zongquan could not break him.
translations.idiomatic: only Chenzhou, barely a hundred li from Cai and very weakly garrisoned, held out. Prefect Zhao Chou fought Zongquan day after day, and Zongquan could not break him.

sentences.zh: 詔以犨為蔡州節度使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Chou military governor of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The throne appointed Chou military governor of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 犨德朱全忠之援，與全忠結婚，凡全忠所調發，無不立至。

translations.literal: Chou was grateful for Zhu Quanzhong's aid; he formed a marriage alliance with Quanzhong, and whenever Quanzhong requisitioned anything, it arrived without delay.
translations.idiomatic: Chou owed Zhu Quanzhong for his support. They sealed the bond with a marriage alliance, and whenever Quanzhong called for troops or supplies, Chou answered at once.

sentences.zh: 王緒至漳州，以道險糧少，令軍中「無得以老弱自隨，犯者斬！

translations.literal: When Wang Xu reached Zhangzhou, because the route was perilous and provisions scarce, he ordered the army: "No one may bring the old and weak along with him—violators will be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xu reached Zhangzhou, the road was hard and food was scarce. He ordered the army: "No one may bring the old or weak along—violators will be beheaded!

sentences.zh: 」唯王潮兄弟扶其母董氏崎嶇從軍，緒召潮等責之曰：「軍皆有法，未有無法之軍。

translations.literal: " Only the Wang Chao brothers supported their mother, Lady Dong, over the rugged road as they followed the army. Xu summoned Chao and the others and rebuked them: "Every army has laws; there is no army without law.
translations.idiomatic: " Only the Wang Chao brothers supported their mother Lady Dong over the rugged trail as they marched. Xu summoned them and rebuked them: "Every army has laws. There is no army without law.

sentences.zh: 汝違吾令而不誅，是無法也。

translations.literal: You violated my order yet are not executed—this is lawlessness.
translations.idiomatic: You broke my order and are not punished—that is lawlessness.

sentences.zh: 」三子曰：「人皆有母，未有無母之人；

translations.literal: " The three brothers said: "Every person has a mother; there is no person without a mother;
translations.idiomatic: " The three brothers replied: "Every man has a mother. There is no man without a mother;

sentences.zh: 將軍奈何使人棄其母！

translations.literal: how can the general make men abandon their mothers!
translations.idiomatic: how can you order men to abandon their mothers!

sentences.zh: 」緒怒，命斬其母。

translations.literal: " Xu grew angry and ordered their mother beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu flew into a rage and ordered their mother executed.

sentences.zh: 三子曰：「潮等事母如事將軍，既殺其母，安用其子！

translations.literal: The three brothers said: "Chao and the others serve our mother as we serve the general. If you kill our mother, what use are her sons!
translations.idiomatic: The brothers said: "We serve our mother as we serve you, General. If you kill our mother, what need have you of her sons!

sentences.zh: 請先母死。

translations.literal: We ask to die before our mother.
translations.idiomatic: Let us die before her.

sentences.zh: 」將士皆為之請，乃捨之。

translations.literal: " The officers and soldiers all pleaded for them, and he spared them.
translations.idiomatic: " The officers and men all pleaded for them, and Xu relented.

sentences.zh: 有望氣者謂緒曰：「軍中有王者氣。

translations.literal: A practitioner of qi divination told Xu: "There is the aura of a king in the army.
translations.idiomatic: A diviner told Xu: "There is royal qi in this army.

sentences.zh: 」於是緒見將卒有勇略逾己及氣質魁岸者皆殺之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon, whenever Xu saw officers and soldiers whose courage and strategy surpassed his own, or whose bearing was imposing, he killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on, Xu killed every officer or soldier he saw who was braver or cleverer than he, or who had the bearing of a leader.

sentences.zh: 劉行全亦死，眾皆自危，曰：「行全親也，且軍鋒之冠，猶不免，況吾屬乎！

translations.literal: Liu Xingquan also died. Everyone felt endangered and said: "Xingquan was a kinsman and the foremost spearhead of the army, yet even he did not escape—how much less the likes of us!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xingquan was killed too. The men grew fearful and said: "Xingquan was a kinsman and the army's finest fighter, yet even he was not spared—what hope have the rest of us!

sentences.zh: 」行至南安，王潮說其前鋒將曰：「吾屬違墳墓，捐妻子，羈旅外鄉為群盜，豈所欲哉！

translations.literal: " When they reached Nan'an, Wang Chao persuaded the vanguard general: "We have left our ancestral graves, abandoned our wives and children, and wandered as exiles in foreign lands to become bandits—is this what we wanted!
translations.idiomatic: " At Nan'an, Wang Chao spoke to the vanguard general: "We left our graves, abandoned our wives and children, and wandered as exiles to become bandits—is that what any of us wanted!

sentences.zh: 乃為緒所迫脅故也。

translations.literal: It is because we were forced and coerced by Xu.
translations.idiomatic: We were driven to it by Xu.

sentences.zh: 今緒猜刻不仁，妄殺無辜，軍中孑孓者受誅且盡。

translations.literal: Now Xu is suspicious, harsh, and unkind; he kills the innocent at will, and those in the army who stand alone are being executed to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xu is suspicious, cruel, and unjust. He kills at whim, and every man without protection in this army is being slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 子鬚眉若神，騎射絕倫，又為前鋒，吾竊為子危之！

translations.literal: You, sir, have brows and beard like a god, and your horsemanship and archery are unmatched; moreover you are vanguard—I privately fear for you!
translations.idiomatic: You look like a god, your riding and shooting are unmatched, and you lead the vanguard—I fear for your life!

sentences.zh: 」前鋒將執潮手泣，問計安出。

translations.literal: " The vanguard general took Chao's hand and wept, asking where the plan would come from.
translations.idiomatic: " The vanguard general seized Chao's hand in tears and asked what could be done.

sentences.zh: 潮為之謀，伏壯士數十人於篁竹中，伺緒至，挺劍大呼躍出，就馬上擒之，反縛以徇，軍中皆呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Chao devised a plan for him: several dozen strong men were hidden in bamboo groves; when Xu arrived, they drew swords, shouted, and leapt out, seized him on horseback, bound him with arms reversed, and paraded him through the camp. The whole army shouted "Long live!
translations.idiomatic: Chao laid a plan: several dozen strong men hid in the bamboo groves. When Xu arrived, they leapt out with drawn swords, seized him from his horse, bound his arms behind him, and paraded him through the camp. The army shouted "Long live!

sentences.zh: 潮推前鋒將為主，前鋒將曰：「吾屬今日不為魚肉，皆王君力也。

translations.literal: Chao urged the vanguard general to take command. The vanguard general said: "Today we are not fish and meat on the chopping block—all thanks to Lord Wang's effort.
translations.idiomatic: Chao urged the vanguard general to take command. The general replied: "Today we are not meat on the block—that is all Lord Wang's doing.

sentences.zh: 天以王君為主，誰敢先之！

translations.literal: Heaven has made Lord Wang our leader—who would dare go before him!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has chosen Lord Wang—who would dare take precedence over him!

sentences.zh: 」相推讓數四，卒奉潮為將軍。

translations.literal: " They pushed deference back and forth several times, and in the end made Chao general.
translations.idiomatic: " They argued back and forth several times, and in the end made Chao their general.

sentences.zh: 緒歎曰：「此子在吾網中不能殺，豈非天哉！

translations.literal: Xu sighed and said: "This boy was in my net and I could not kill him—is this not Heaven's will!
translations.idiomatic: Xu sighed: "This man was in my grasp and I could not kill him—is that not Heaven's doing!

sentences.zh: 」潮引兵將還光州，約其屬，所過秋豪無犯。

translations.literal: " Chao led his troops intending to return to Guangzhou, and pledged to his followers that wherever they passed they would not violate even the slightest thing.
translations.idiomatic: " Chao led his men back toward Guangzhou and pledged that they would not take so much as a blade of grass along the way.

sentences.zh: 行及沙縣，泉州人張延魯等以刺史廖彥若貪暴，帥耆老奉牛酒遮道，請潮留為州將，潮乃引兵圍泉州。

translations.literal: When they reached Shaxian, Zhang Yanlu and others of Quanzhou, because Prefect Liao Yanruo was greedy and brutal, led elders bearing oxen and wine to block the road and asked Chao to stay on as the prefecture's commander. Chao then led troops to besiege Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaxian, Zhang Yanlu and other men of Quanzhou—fed up with the greedy, brutal prefect Liao Yanruo—led elders with oxen and wine to block the road and begged Chao to stay and lead the prefecture. Chao then marched to besiege Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊申，以陳敬瑄為三川及峽內諸州指揮、制置等使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wushen day, Chen Jingxuan was appointed commissioner for directing and organizing the Three Gorges region and all prefectures within the gorges.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wushen day, Chen Jingxuan was appointed commissioner for the Three Gorges and all prefectures within the gorges.

sentences.zh: 蔡軍圍荊南，馬步使趙匡謀奉前節度使陳儒以出，留後張瑰覺之，殺匡及儒。

translations.literal: The Cai army besieged Jingnan. Zhao Kuang, commissioner of cavalry and infantry, plotted to install the former military governor Chen Ru to break out. Acting military governor Zhang Gui discovered it and killed Kuang and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: The Cai army besieged Jingnan. Zhao Kuang, commissioner of cavalry and infantry, plotted to restore the former governor Chen Ru and break out. Acting governor Zhang Gui discovered the plot and killed both Kuang and Ru.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸丑，秦宗權敗朱全忠於八角。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on guichou day, Qin Zongquan defeated Zhu Quanzhong at Bajiao.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on guichou day, Qin Zongquan defeated Zhu Quanzhong at Bajiao.

sentences.zh: 王重榮求救於李克用，克用方怨朝廷不罪朱全忠，選兵市馬，聚結諸胡，議攻汴州，報曰：「待吾先滅全忠，還掃鼠輩如秋葉耳！

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong asked Li Keyong for rescue. Keyong was then resentful that the court had not punished Zhu Quanzhong; he selected troops, bought horses, gathered the various Hu peoples, and discussed attacking Bianzhou. He replied: "Wait until I first destroy Quanzhong; then on my return I shall sweep away vermin like you as easily as autumn leaves!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong appealed to Li Keyong for help. Keyong was still angry that the court had not punished Zhu Quanzhong. He was raising troops, buying horses, and rallying the frontier tribes for an attack on Bianzhou. He answered: "Wait until I destroy Quanzhong first. When I return, I will sweep vermin like you aside as easily as autumn leaves!

sentences.zh: 」重榮曰：「待公自關東還，吾為虜矣。

translations.literal: " Chongrong said: "By the time you return from east of the Pass, I will already be a captive.
translations.idiomatic: " Chongrong replied: "By the time you return from the east, I will already be a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 不若先除君側之惡，退擒全忠易矣。

translations.literal: Better first remove the evil at the ruler's side; then on withdrawal capturing Quanzhong will be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Better to remove the evil at the emperor's side first. Then Quanzhong will be easy to take.

sentences.zh: 」時朱玫、李昌符亦陰附朱全忠，克用乃上言：「玫、昌符與全忠相表裡，欲共滅臣，臣不得不自救，已集蕃、漢兵十五萬，決以來年濟河，自謂北討二鎮；

translations.literal: At this time Zhu Mei and Li Changfu were also secretly allied with Zhu Quanzhong, so Keyong submitted a memorial saying: "Mei and Changfu act in concert with Quanzhong, intending jointly to destroy me. I have no choice but to save myself. I have already assembled 150,000 barbarian and Han troops and am resolved to cross the Yellow River next year; I call this a northern expedition against the two garrison commands;
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhu Mei and Li Changfu had also thrown in secretly with Zhu Quanzhong. Keyong memorialized the throne: "Mei and Changfu are Quanzhong's partners inside and out; together they mean to destroy me. I must save myself. I have already gathered 150,000 barbarian and Chinese troops and mean to cross the Yellow River next year on what I will call a northern campaign against the two commands;

sentences.zh: 不近京城，保無掠擾。

translations.literal: I shall not approach the capital; I guarantee there will be no looting or disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: I will not come near the capital, and I pledge there will be no plunder or disorder.

sentences.zh: 既誅二鎮，乃旋師滅全忠以雪仇恥。

translations.literal: Once the two garrisons are eliminated, I shall then turn my army and destroy Quanzhong to wash away my enmity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: After I have eliminated the two commands, I will turn my army and destroy Quanzhong to settle the score.

sentences.zh: 」上遣使者諭釋，冠蓋相望。

translations.literal: " The emperor sent envoys to explain and mollify him; official carriages and canopied vehicles lined the road one after another.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent envoy after envoy to explain the court's position and mollify him; the road was crowded with official escorts.

sentences.zh: 朱玫欲朝廷討克用，數遣人潛入京城，燒積聚，或刺殺近侍，聲雲克用所為。

translations.literal: Zhu Mei wished the court to attack Keyong. He repeatedly sent men secretly into the capital to burn stored goods, or to assassinate close attendants, claiming it was Keyong's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei wanted the court to move against Keyong. Again and again he sent agents into the capital to burn stores or murder palace attendants, then blamed it on Keyong.

sentences.zh: 於是京師震恐，日有訛言。

translations.literal: The capital thus trembled in fear, and each day brought new rumors.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was shaken with fear, and wild rumors circulated daily.

sentences.zh: 令孜遣玫、昌符將本軍及神策鄜、延、靈、夏等軍各三萬人屯沙苑，以討王重榮。

translations.literal: Lingci dispatched Mei and Changfu to lead their own armies and the Shence, Bin, Yan, Ling, and Xia armies, thirty thousand men each, to encamp at Shayuan to attack Wang Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: Lingci sent Mei and Changfu with their own forces plus thirty thousand men apiece from the Shence and the Bin, Yan, Ling, and Xia commands to camp at Shayuan and attack Wang Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 重榮發兵拒之，告急於李克用，克用引兵赴之。

translations.literal: Chongrong raised troops to resist them and sent urgent appeals to Li Keyong; Keyong led his army to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong marched out to meet them and begged Li Keyong for help. Keyong brought his army to join him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，重榮遣兵攻同州，刺史郭璋出戰，敗死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Chongrong sent troops to attack Tong Prefecture. Prefect Guo Zhang went out to fight and was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Chongrong attacked Tongzhou. Prefect Guo Zhang fought and was killed in defeat.

sentences.zh: 重榮與玫等相守月餘，克用兵至，與重榮俱壁沙苑，表請誅令孜及玫、昌符。

translations.literal: Chongrong and Mei and the others faced each other in stalemate for more than a month. When Keyong's troops arrived, he and Chongrong together fortified Shayuan and submitted a memorial requesting execution of Lingci and Mei and Changfu.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong and Mei's forces faced off for over a month. When Keyong arrived, he and Chongrong fortified Shayuan together and memorialized the throne demanding the execution of Lingci, Mei, and Changfu.
