sentences.zh: 詔和解之，克用不聽。

translations.literal: An edict ordered reconciliation; Keyong would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a settlement; Keyong refused.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸酉，合戰，玫、昌符大敗，各走還本鎮，潰軍所過焚掠。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on guiyou day, the armies joined battle. Mei and Changfu were utterly defeated and each fled back to his home garrison. The broken troops burned and pillaged wherever they passed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guiyou day, the armies clashed. Mei and Changfu were routed and each fled to his own command, while their fleeing soldiers burned and looted the countryside.

sentences.zh: 克用進逼京城，乙亥夜，令孜奉天子自開遠門出幸鳳翔。

translations.literal: Keyong pressed toward the capital. On the night of yihai day, Lingci escorted the Son of Heaven out through Kaiyuan Gate on a progress to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong advanced on the capital. On the night of yihai, Lingci fled with the emperor through Kaiyuan Gate toward Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 初，黃巢焚長安宮室而去，諸道兵入城縱掠，焚府寺民居什六七，王徽累年補葺，僅完一二，至是復為亂兵焚掠，無孑遺矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Huang Chao had burned Chang'an's palaces and departed. Troops from various circuits entered the city and plundered freely, burning government offices, temples, and private dwellings—six or seven tenths. Wang Hui had spent years repairing; only one or two tenths had been restored. Now they were again burned and plundered by disorderly troops, with nothing left standing.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao had first torched Chang'an's palaces and left, soldiers from every circuit had marched in and looted freely, destroying six or seven tenths of the government offices, temples, and homes. Wang Hui had spent years rebuilding; barely a tenth had been restored. Now disorderly troops burned and plundered again until nothing survived.

sentences.zh: 是歲，賜河中軍號護國。

translations.literal: That year, the Hezhong army was granted the designation Huguo ("Protecting the State").
translations.idiomatic: That year the Hezhong garrison was given the name Huguo—Protecting the State.

sentences.zh: 僖宗惠聖恭定孝皇帝下之上光啟二年（

translations.literal: Below [the account of] Emperor Xizong Huisheng Gongding Xiaoxiao, Part One: second year of Guangqi (
translations.idiomatic: [Accounts of] Emperor Xizong Huisheng Gongding Xiaoxiao, Part One — second year of Guangqi (

sentences.zh: 丙午，公元八八六年）

translations.literal: bingwu, equivalent to 886 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingwu, corresponding to 886 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，鎮海牙將張郁作亂，攻陷常州。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Zhang Yu, a garrison officer of Zhenhai, rebelled and captured Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Zhang Yu, a garrison officer of Zhenhai, raised a rebellion and seized Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 李克用還軍河中，與王重榮同表請大駕還宮，因罪狀田令孜，請誅之。

translations.literal: Li Keyong returned his army to Hezhong and jointly submitted a memorial with Wang Chongrong requesting the imperial carriage's return to the palace, thereby listing Tian Lingci's crimes and requesting his execution.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong withdrew to Hezhong and joined Wang Chongrong in a memorial begging the emperor to return to the capital, listing Tian Lingci's crimes and calling for his death.

sentences.zh: 上復以飛龍使楊復恭為樞密使。

translations.literal: The emperor again appointed Flying Dragon Commissioner Yang Fugong as Military Affairs Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor restored Yang Fugong, commissioner of the Flying Dragon Office, as commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 戊子，令孜請上幸興元，上不從。

translations.literal: On wuzi day, Lingci requested that the emperor proceed to Xingyuan; the emperor refused.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day, Lingci urged the emperor to go to Xingyuan; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 是夜，令孜引兵入宮，劫上幸寶雞，黃門衛士從者才數百人，宰相朝臣皆不知。

translations.literal: That night, Lingci led troops into the palace, seized the emperor and forced a progress to Baoji. Only a few hundred eunuch guards followed; the chief ministers and court officials knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: That night Lingci marched into the palace with troops, abducted the emperor, and forced him toward Baoji. Only a few hundred eunuch guards followed—the chief ministers and court officials knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士承旨杜讓能宿直禁中，聞之，步追乘輿，出城十餘里，得人所遺馬，無羈勒，解帶繫頸而乘之，獨追及上於寶雞。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Expositor Du Rangneng was on night duty in the palace. When he heard, he ran after the imperial carriage. Beyond the walls more than ten li, he found an abandoned horse with no bridle or reins; he undid his belt, tied it around the horse's neck, mounted, and alone caught up with the emperor at Baoji.
translations.idiomatic: Du Rangneng, senior Hanlin academician, was on night duty in the palace. Hearing what had happened, he ran after the imperial carriage. More than ten li outside the walls he found an abandoned horse with no bridle; he tied his sash around its neck, mounted, and rode alone until he caught up with the emperor at Baoji.

sentences.zh: 明日，乃有太子少保孔緯等數人繼至。

translations.literal: The next day, a few men including Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent Kong Wei arrived in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the next day did a handful of officials, including Junior Tutor to the Heir Kong Wei, straggle in.

sentences.zh: 讓能，審權之子；

translations.literal: Rangneng was the son of Shen Quan;
translations.idiomatic: Rangneng was Shen Quan's son;

sentences.zh: 緯，戣之孫也。

translations.literal: Wei was the grandson of Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was Mao's grandson.

sentences.zh: 宗正奉太廟神主至鄠，遇盜，皆失之。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Clan, bearing the ancestral tablets from the imperial temple, reached E Prefecture, encountered bandits, and lost them all.
translations.idiomatic: The director of the imperial clan, carrying the spirit tablets from the ancestral temple, reached Ezhou but was robbed by bandits and lost them all.

sentences.zh: 朝士追乘輿者至盩厔，為亂兵所掠，衣裝殆盡。

translations.literal: Court officials pursuing the imperial carriage reached Zhouzhi and were plundered by disorderly troops; their clothes and baggage were nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials chasing the imperial retinue reached Zhouzhi, where disorderly soldiers stripped them of nearly everything they had.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，上以孔緯為御史大夫，使還召百官，上留寶雞以待之。

translations.literal: On gengyin day, the emperor appointed Kong Wei Censor-in-Chief and sent him back to summon the officials; the emperor remained at Baoji to await them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day the emperor named Kong Wei censor-in-chief and sent him back to summon the rest of the court. The emperor stayed at Baoji to wait.

sentences.zh: 時田令孜弄權，再致播遷，天下共忿疾之。

translations.literal: At this time Tian Lingci wielded power; he had twice caused the court's exile, and all under Heaven hated him together.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingci was wielding power; he had twice driven the court into exile, and the empire seethed with resentment against him.

sentences.zh: 朱玫、李昌符亦恥為之用，且憚李克用、王重榮之強，更與之合。

translations.literal: Zhu Mei and Li Changfu also felt shame at being used by him, and feared the strength of Li Keyong and Wang Chongrong; they again joined with them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei and Li Changfu were ashamed to serve him and feared the power of Li Keyong and Wang Chongrong—they switched sides again and joined Keyong and Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 蕭遘因邠寧奏事判官李松年至鳳翔，遣召朱玫亟迎車駕，癸巳，玫引步騎五千至鳳翔。

translations.literal: Xiao Xiong, through Li Songnian, memorial affairs judge of Binning, who had come to Fengxiang, dispatched a summons for Zhu Mei to hurry and welcome the imperial carriage. On guisi day, Mei led five thousand infantry and cavalry to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Songnian, memorial affairs judge for Binning, arrived at Fengxiang, Xiao Xiong sent word urging Zhu Mei to hurry and welcome the emperor. On guisi day Mei marched in with five thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 孔緯詣宰相，欲宣詔召之，蕭遘、裴澈以令孜在上側，不欲往，辭疾不見。

translations.literal: Kong Wei went to the chief ministers, intending to proclaim an edict summoning them. Xiao Xiong and Pei Che, because Lingci was at the emperor's side, did not wish to go; they pleaded illness and refused to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wei went to the chief ministers to issue an edict summoning the officials back. Xiao Xiong and Pei Che, with Lingci at the emperor's elbow, would not go—they pleaded illness and refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 緯令台吏趣百官詣行在，皆辭以無袍笏，緯召三院御史，泣謂：「布衣親舊有急，猶當赴之。

translations.literal: Wei ordered the censorate clerks to urge the officials to the temporary court; all excused themselves saying they had no court robes or tally boards. Wei summoned the censors of the three bureaus and wept, saying: "When a commoner's friend or relative is in distress, one still ought to go.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ordered censorate clerks to hurry the officials to the emperor's camp. All pleaded that they had no court dress or ceremonial tablets. Wei summoned the censors of all three bureaus and wept: "When a commoner's friend falls into trouble, one still goes to help.

sentences.zh: 豈有天子蒙塵，為人臣子，累召而不往者！

translations.literal: How can there be those summoned again and again who refuse to go, when the Son of Heaven suffers dust on the road, and they are his ministers and subjects!
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the Son of Heaven himself is driven into exile, can his ministers refuse call after call to attend him?

sentences.zh: 」御史請辦裝數日而行，緯拂衣起曰：「吾妻病垂死且不顧，諸君善自為謀，請從此辭！

translations.literal: " The censors asked for several days to prepare their gear before departing. Wei brushed his robes and rose, saying: "My wife lies near death and I do not even attend to her. You gentlemen may look after yourselves—I take my leave here!
translations.idiomatic: " The censors asked for a few days to pack. Wei shook out his sleeves and stood. "My own wife lies dying and I have abandoned her. Look after yourselves—I am done with you!

sentences.zh: 」乃詣李昌符，請騎衛送至行在，昌符義之，贈裝錢，遣騎送之。

translations.literal: " He then went to Li Changfu, requesting escort cavalry to deliver him to the temporary court. Changfu admired his integrity, gave him travel money, and dispatched cavalry to see him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: " He went to Li Changfu and asked for an escort to the emperor's camp. Changfu respected his loyalty, gave him travel funds, and sent horsemen to convey him there.

sentences.zh: 瑄寧、鳳翔兵追逼乘輿，敗神策指揮使楊晟於潘氏，鉦鼓之聲聞於行宮。

translations.literal: Binning and Fengxiang troops pressed upon the imperial carriage, defeated Shence Commander Yang Sheng at Panshi; the sound of gongs and drums reached the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from Binning and Fengxiang closed on the imperial retinue and defeated Shence commander Yang Sheng at Panshi—the clamor of drums and gongs echoed to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 田令孜奉上發寶雞，留禁軍守石鼻為後拒。

translations.literal: Tian Lingci escorted the emperor to depart from Baoji, leaving the palace guard to hold Shibi as rear resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Lingci hurried the emperor out of Baoji, leaving palace troops at Shibi to cover the rear.

sentences.zh: 置感義軍於興、鳳二州，以楊晟為節度使，守散關。

translations.literal: He established the Ganyi army in Xing and Feng Prefectures, appointing Yang Sheng military governor to guard Sanguan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He created the Ganyi command across Xing and Feng prefectures and made Yang Sheng its military governor to hold Sanguan Pass.

sentences.zh: 時軍民雜糅，鋒鏑縱橫，以神策軍使王建、晉暉為清道斬斫使，建以長劍五百前驅奮擊，乘輿乃得前。

translations.literal: At this time soldiers and civilians were intermixed, blades and arrows flying everywhere. The emperor appointed Shence commissioners Wang Jian and Jin Hui as commissioners for clearing the road by cutting down [obstacles]. Jian led five hundred with long swords as vanguard, fighting fiercely, and the imperial carriage was able to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians were tangled together; steel flashed on every side. The emperor named Shence officers Wang Jian and Jin Hui commissioners for clearing the road. Jian drove five hundred swordsmen at the van, hacking a path forward so the retinue could move.

sentences.zh: 上以傳國寶授建使負之以從，登大散嶺。

translations.literal: The emperor entrusted the imperial seal of transmission to Jian, ordering him to carry it and follow, and they ascended Dasan Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor handed Wang Jian the imperial seal and bade him carry it at his side as they climbed Dasan Ridge.

sentences.zh: 李昌符焚閣道丈餘，將摧折，王建扶掖上自煙焰中躍過。

translations.literal: Li Changfu burned more than a ten-foot section of the plank road, which was about to collapse. Wang Jian supported the emperor as he leapt through from amid smoke and flame.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changfu had burned a section of the cliff plank road; as it began to give way, Wang Jian braced the emperor and helped him leap through smoke and fire to the far side.

sentences.zh: 夜，宿板下，上枕建膝而寢，既覺，始進食，解御袍賜建曰：「以其有淚痕故也。

translations.literal: At night they lodged beneath the planks. The emperor slept with his head on Jian's knee. When he awoke, he first ate, then removed his imperial robe and bestowed it on Jian, saying: "Because it bears tear-stains.
translations.idiomatic: That night they camped under the cliff road. The emperor slept with his head in Jian's lap. When he woke he ate at last, then took off his robe and gave it to Jian, saying: "It has my tears on it.

sentences.zh: 」車駕才入散關，朱玫已圍寶雞。

translations.literal: " The imperial carriage had just entered Sanguan Pass when Zhu Mei had already besieged Baoji.
translations.idiomatic: " The retinue had barely passed through Sanguan when Zhu Mei was already besieging Baoji.

sentences.zh: 石鼻軍潰，玫長驅攻散關，不克。

translations.literal: The Shibi garrison collapsed. Mei drove straight at Sanguan Pass but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison at Shibi broke. Mei drove hard for Sanguan Pass but failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 嗣襄王熅，肅宗之玄孫也，有疾，從上不及，留遵塗驛，為玫所得，與俱還鳳翔。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiang, heir to the line, Yun, a great-great-grandson of Emperor Suzong, was ill and could not keep pace with the emperor. He remained at Zuntu Post Station and was captured by Mei, who took him back to Fengxiang together.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yun of Xiang—a great-great-grandson of Emperor Suzong—was ill and could not keep up. He was left at Zuntu Post, captured by Mei, and carried back to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，李克用還太原。

translations.literal: On gengxu day, Li Keyong returned to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day, Li Keyong withdrew to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 二月，王重榮、朱政、李昌符復上表請誅田令孜。

translations.literal: In the second month, Wang Chongrong, Zhu Zheng, and Li Changfu again submitted memorials requesting execution of Tian Lingci.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Wang Chongrong, Zhu Mei, and Li Changfu again memorialized the throne demanding Tian Lingci's death.

sentences.zh: 以前東都留守鄭從讜為守太傅兼侍中。

translations.literal: Former eastern capital intendant Zheng Congdang was appointed Guardian Grand Tutor and concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Former Luoyang intendant Zheng Congdang was named guardian grand tutor and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 朱玫、李昌符使山南西道節度使石君涉柵絕險要，燒郵驛，上由它道以進。

translations.literal: Zhu Mei and Li Changfu had the Shannan West Circuit military governor Shi Junshe barricade strategic passes, burn post stations, and force the emperor to advance by another route.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei and Li Changfu ordered Shannan West governor Shi Junshe to block the mountain passes, burn the post stations, and force the emperor onto another road.

sentences.zh: 山谷崎嶇，邠軍迫其後，危殆者數四，僅得達山南。

translations.literal: The mountain valleys were rugged; Binning troops pressed from the rear. Four times they were nearly lost; they barely reached Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain paths were treacherous and Binning troops pressed from behind. Four times they nearly perished before barely reaching Shannan.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬午，石君涉棄鎮逃歸朱玫。

translations.literal: In the third month, on renwu day, Shi Junshe abandoned his post and fled back to Zhu Mei.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renwu day, Shi Junshe abandoned his command and fled to Zhu Mei.

sentences.zh: 癸未，鳳翔百官蕭遘等罪狀田令孜及其黨韋昭度，請誅之。

translations.literal: On guiwei day, the Fengxiang officials led by Xiao Xiong listed the crimes of Tian Lingci and his faction member Wei Zhaodu and requested their execution.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day the Fengxiang officials, led by Xiao Xiong, indicted Tian Lingci and his ally Wei Zhaodu and called for their execution.

sentences.zh: 初，昭度因供奉僧澈結宦官，得為相。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhaodu had gained the chancellorship by cultivating eunuchs through the tribute monk Che.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu had earlier won the chancellorship by currying favor with the eunuchs through the tribute monk Che.

sentences.zh: 澈師知玄鄙澈所為，昭度每與同列詣知玄，皆拜之，知玄揖使詣澈啜茶。

translations.literal: Che's teacher Zhixuan despised what Che did. Whenever Zhaodu went with his colleagues to visit Zhixuan, they all bowed to him; Zhixuan would bow in return and send them on to Che for tea.
translations.idiomatic: Che's teacher Zhixuan scorned his disciple's conduct. Whenever Zhaodu and his fellow ministers visited Zhixuan they bowed low; Zhixuan bowed back and directed them to Che for tea.

sentences.zh: 山南西道監軍馮翊嚴遵美迎上於西縣，丙申，車駕至興元。

translations.literal: Shannan West Circuit supervisory commissioner Yan Zunmei of Fenyang welcomed the emperor at Xixian. On bingshen day the imperial carriage reached Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zunmei, supervisory commissioner of Shannan West, welcomed the emperor at Xixian. On bingshen day the retinue reached Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以御史大夫孔緯、翰林學士承旨、兵部尚書杜讓能並為兵部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On wuxu day, Censor-in-Chief Kong Wei and Hanlin Academician Expositor and Minister of War Du Rangneng were all appointed Vice Ministers of War and Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day Kong Wei, censor-in-chief, and Du Rangneng, senior Hanlin academician and minister of war, were both made vice ministers of war and grand councilors.

sentences.zh: 保鑾都將李鋋等敗邠軍於鳳州。

translations.literal: Imperial Guard generals Li Qian and others defeated the Binning army at Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial guard generals Li Qian and others routed the Binning army at Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔加王重榮應接糧料使，使調本道谷十五萬斛以濟國用。

translations.literal: An edict added Wang Chongrong as commissioner for receiving and dispatching grain supplies, ordering him to levy 150,000 shi of grain from his circuit to support state expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named Wang Chongrong commissioner for grain supply and ordered him to levy 150,000 shi of grain from his circuit for the court's use.

sentences.zh: 重榮表稱令孜未誅，不奉詔。

translations.literal: Chongrong submitted a memorial saying that as long as Lingci was not executed, he would not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong replied that until Lingci was dead he would not comply.

sentences.zh: 以尚書左丞盧渥為戶部尚書，充山南西道留後。

translations.literal: Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat Lu Wo was appointed Minister of Revenue and acting governor of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wo, left vice minister of the secretariat, was made minister of revenue and acting governor of Shannan West.

sentences.zh: 以嚴遵美為內樞密使，遣王建帥部兵戍三泉，晉暉及神策使張造帥四都兵屯黑水，修棧道以通往來。

translations.literal: Yan Zunmei was appointed Inner Military Affairs Commissioner. Wang Jian was dispatched to garrison Sanquan with his troops; Jin Hui and Shence commissioner Zhang Zao led the four capital armies to encamp at Heishui and repair the plank roads for traffic.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zunmei was named inner commissioner of military affairs. Wang Jian was sent to garrison Sanquan; Jin Hui and Shence officer Zhang Zao camped at Heishui with the four capital armies and rebuilt the plank roads.

sentences.zh: 以建遙領壁州刺史。

translations.literal: Jian was given titular appointment as prefect of Bi Prefecture from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was given the distant title of prefect of Bizhou.

sentences.zh: 將帥遙領州鎮自此始。

translations.literal: From this began the practice of generals holding prefectures and garrisons in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: Generals holding provincial commands from afar began with this.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄疑東川節度使高仁厚，欲去之。

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan suspected Dongchuan military governor Gao Renhou and wished to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan grew suspicious of Dongchuan governor Gao Renhou and wanted him gone.

sentences.zh: 遂州刺史鄭君立起兵攻陷漢州，進向成都。

translations.literal: Suizhou Prefect Zheng Junli raised troops, captured Han Prefecture, and advanced toward Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Junli, prefect of Suizhou, raised troops, seized Hanzhou, and marched on Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄遣其將李順之逆戰，君立敗死。

translations.literal: Jingxuan sent his general Li Shunzhi to meet him in battle; Junli was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan sent his general Li Shunzhi to intercept him; Junli was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄又發維、茂羌軍擊仁厚，殺之。

translations.literal: Jingxuan also sent Wei and Mao tribal troops to attack Renhou and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan then sent Wei and Mao tribal forces against Renhou and killed him.

sentences.zh: 朱玫以田令孜在天子左右，終不可去，言於蕭遘曰：「主上播遷六年，中原將士冒矢石，百姓供饋餉，戰死餓死，什減七八，僅得復京城。

translations.literal: Because Tian Lingci was at the Son of Heaven's side and could never be removed, Zhu Mei said to Xiao Xiong: "The sovereign has been driven into exile for six years. Soldiers of the central plains have braved arrows and stones; the people have supplied provisions. Those killed in battle or starved to death—seven or eight tenths are gone. We barely recovered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei, seeing that Tian Lingci still clung to the emperor's side and could not be dislodged, told Xiao Xiong: "For six years the sovereign has wandered in exile. Soldiers of the heartland have faced arrows and stone; the people have fed the armies. Seven or eight in ten have died in battle or of hunger—we barely won the capital back.

sentences.zh: 天下方喜車駕還宮，主上更以勤王之功為敕使之榮，委以大權，使墮綱紀，騷擾籓鎮，召亂生禍。

translations.literal: All under Heaven rejoiced that the imperial carriage would return to the palace, yet the sovereign instead made the eunuch's service in rallying troops a source of glory, entrusted him with great power, let him overturn law and order, harass the garrison commands, and summon chaos and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The empire rejoiced to see the court return home, yet the emperor rewarded the eunuch's 'loyal service' with supreme power—letting him wreck discipline, harry the provinces, and bring chaos down on us all.

sentences.zh: 玫昨奉尊命來迎大駕，不蒙信察，反類脅君。

translations.literal: Yesterday I obeyed your honored command to welcome the imperial carriage, yet received no trust; instead I was treated like one coercing his sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I came at your order to welcome the emperor, and instead of trust I was treated like a kidnapper.

sentences.zh: 吾輩報國之心極矣，戰賊之力殫矣，安能垂頭弭耳，受制於閽寺之手哉！

translations.literal: Our devotion to the state is at its utmost; our strength for fighting rebels is exhausted. How can we hang our heads and fold our ears, submitting to control by palace eunuchs!
translations.idiomatic: We have given everything to the throne; we have spent ourselves fighting rebels. How can we bow our heads and submit to eunuch masters?

sentences.zh: 李氏孫尚多，相公盍改圖以利社稷乎？

translations.literal: There are still many descendants of the Li house. Chancellor, why not change your plan for the good of the realm?
translations.idiomatic: The Li clan still has heirs. Chancellor, why not change course for the realm's sake?

sentences.zh: 」遘曰：「主上踐阼十餘年，無大過惡。

translations.literal: " Xiong said: "The sovereign has reigned more than ten years without great faults or wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiong replied: "The emperor has reigned more than ten years without grave fault.

sentences.zh: 正以令孜專權肘腋，致坐不安席，上每言之，流涕不已。

translations.literal: It is only that Lingci monopolizes power at his elbow, causing him to sit uneasily. Whenever the sovereign speaks of it, he weeps without cease.
translations.idiomatic: It is Lingci's monopoly of power at his side that keeps him from resting easy—the emperor weeps whenever he speaks of it.

sentences.zh: 近日上初無行意，令孜陳兵帳前，迫脅以行，不容俟旦。

translations.literal: Recently the sovereign at first had no intention of departing; Lingci arrayed troops before the tent and coerced him to go, not allowing him to wait until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the emperor did not even wish to leave; Lingci lined troops before his tent and forced him out before daybreak.

sentences.zh: 罪皆在令孜，人誰不知！

translations.literal: The guilt is all Lingci's—who does not know this!
translations.idiomatic: The blame is all Lingci's—everyone knows it!

sentences.zh: 足下盡心王室，正有引兵還鎮，拜表迎鑾。

translations.literal: You, sir, should devote yourself to the royal house; the proper course is to lead your troops back to your garrison and submit a memorial welcoming the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Serve the throne faithfully: march your troops home and memorial the emperor to return.

sentences.zh: 廢立重事，伊、霍所難，遘不敢聞命！

translations.literal: Deposing and enthroning are weighty matters—even Yi and Huo found them difficult. Xiong dare not accept your command!
translations.idiomatic: Deposing and enthroning an emperor is grave business—even Yi Yin and Huo Guang shrank from it. I cannot obey you!

sentences.zh: 」玫出，宣言曰：「我立李氏一王，敢異議者斬！

translations.literal: " Mei went out and proclaimed: "I shall establish one prince of the Li house. Whoever dares object will be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: " Mei left and declared: "I will set up a Li prince. Anyone who objects dies!

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬子，玫逼鳳翔百官奉襄王熅權監軍國事，承製封拜指揮，仍遣大臣入蜀迎駕，盟百官於石鼻驛。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renzi day, Mei forced the Fengxiang officials to install Prince Yun of Xiang as regent over state and military affairs, issuing edicts for appointments and dismissals. He still sent chief ministers into Shu to welcome the imperial carriage, and swore an oath with the officials at Shibi Post Station.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on renzi day, Mei forced the Fengxiang officials to install Prince Yun of Xiang as regent, with authority to appoint and dismiss by edict. He sent ministers into Shu to welcome the emperor and bound the officials in oath at Shibi Post.

sentences.zh: 玫使蕭遘為冊文，遘辭以文思荒落；

translations.literal: Mei had Xiao Xiong compose the investiture document; Xiong declined, saying his literary talent was withered.
translations.idiomatic: Mei asked Xiao Xiong to draft the investiture edict; Xiong pleaded that his literary powers had failed him.

sentences.zh: 乃使兵部侍郎判戶部鄭昌圖為之。

translations.literal: He then had Vice Minister of War and Acting Minister of Revenue Zheng Changtu compose it.
translations.idiomatic: Mei turned to Zheng Changtu, vice minister of war acting as minister of revenue, to write it instead.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，熅受冊，玫自兼左、右神策十軍使，帥百官奉熅還京師；

translations.literal: On yimao day, Yun received investiture. Mei personally added the posts of commissioner of the Left and Right Shence Ten Armies, and led the officials escorting Yun back to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day Yun was invested. Mei made himself commissioner of the Left and Right Shence Ten Armies and led the officials escorting Yun back to the capital;

sentences.zh: 以鄭昌圖同平章事、判度支、鹽鐵、戶部，各置副使，三司之事一以委焉。

translations.literal: Zheng Changtu was made Grand Councilor and given charge of the treasury, salt and iron, and revenue bureaus, each with a deputy; all affairs of the three offices were entirely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Changtu was made grand councilor with charge of the treasury, salt and iron, and revenue, each with a deputy—all three fiscal offices were placed entirely in his hands.

sentences.zh: 河中百官崔安潛等上襄王箋，賀受冊。

translations.literal: The Hezhong officials led by Cui Anqian submitted a letter to Prince Yun of Xiang congratulating him on receiving investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Anqian and the other Hezhong officials sent Prince Yun a letter congratulating him on his investiture.

sentences.zh: 田令孜自知不為天下所容，乃薦樞密使使楊復恭為左神策中尉、觀軍容使，自除西川監軍使，往依陳敬瑄。

translations.literal: Tian Lingci knew he was no longer tolerated by the world. He recommended Military Affairs Commissioner Yang Fugong as Left Shence Commandant and Army Supervisor, removed himself as West Sichuan supervisory commissioner, and went to rely on Chen Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the empire would no longer tolerate him, Tian Lingci recommended Yang Fugong for commissioner of military affairs and left Shence commandant, stepped down as West Sichuan supervisory commissioner, and went to take refuge with Chen Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 復恭斥令孜之黨，出王建為利州刺史，晉暉為集州刺史，張造為萬州刺史，李師泰為忠州刺史。

translations.literal: Fugong drove out Lingci's faction, sending Wang Jian out as prefect of Li Prefecture, Jin Hui as prefect of Ji Prefecture, Zhang Zao as prefect of Wan Prefecture, and Li Shitai as prefect of Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong purged Lingci's allies, posting Wang Jian to Lizhou, Jin Hui to Jizhou, Zhang Zao to Wanzhou, and Li Shitai to Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，朱玫以中書侍郎、同平章事蕭遘為太子太保，自加侍中、諸道鹽鐵、轉運等使；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Zhu Mei made Palace Attendant and Grand Councilor Xiao Xiong Junior Tutor to the Heir and added for himself the posts of Palace Attendant and commissioner for salt and iron and transport on all circuits;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhu Mei demoted Palace Attendant and Grand Councilor Xiao Xiong to junior tutor to the heir and gave himself the titles of palace attendant and commissioner for salt, iron, and transport on all circuits;

sentences.zh: 加裴澈判度支，鄭昌圖判戶部；

translations.literal: Pei Che was added as acting head of the treasury bureau, and Zheng Changtu as acting head of the revenue bureau;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Che was given acting charge of the treasury bureau and Zheng Changtu of the revenue bureau;

sentences.zh: 以淮南節度使高駢兼中書令，充江、淮鹽鐵、轉運等使、諸道行營兵馬都統；

translations.literal: Huainan military governor Gao Pian was concurrently made Palace Attendant and commissioner for Jiang-Huai salt and iron and transport and overall commander of circuit camp armies;
translations.idiomatic: Huainan governor Gao Pian was made palace attendant, commissioner for Jiang-Huai salt, iron, and transport, and overall commander of circuit armies;

sentences.zh: 淮南右都押牙、和州刺史呂用之為嶺南東道節度使；

translations.literal: Huainan Right Capital Guard Deputy and He Prefecture prefect Lu Yongzhi was made military governor of Lingnan East Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yongzhi, Huainan's right capital guard deputy and prefect of Hezhou, was made governor of Lingnan East;

sentences.zh: 大行封拜以悅籓鎮。

translations.literal: Broad appointments and enfeoffments were made to please the garrison commands.
translations.idiomatic: Titles and posts were handed out lavishly to win over the provinces.

sentences.zh: 遣吏部侍郎夏侯潭宣諭河北，戶部侍郎楊陟宣諭江、淮，諸籓鎮受其命者什六七，高駢仍奉箋勸進。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Xia Houtan was dispatched to announce the court's will in Hebei; Vice Minister of Revenue Yang Zhi to Jiang-Huai. Six or seven tenths of the garrison commands accepted their orders; Gao Pian still submitted a letter urging Yun's enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Xia Houtan was sent to announce the court's will in Hebei; Vice Minister of Revenue Yang Zhi to Jiang-Huai. Six or seven tenths of the provinces accepted the orders; Gao Pian still sent a letter urging Yun to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 呂用之建牙開幕，一與駢同；

translations.literal: Lu Yongzhi established his headquarters and staff on the same scale as Pian's;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yongzhi set up headquarters and a full staff matching Pian's own;

sentences.zh: 凡駢之腹心，及將校能任事者，皆逼以從己，諸所施為，不復咨稟。

translations.literal: All of Pian's trusted men and capable officers and commanders were compelled to follow him; in everything he did he no longer sought approval.
translations.idiomatic: every trusted man and capable officer around Pian was forced into his service, and he stopped consulting Pian on anything he did.

sentences.zh: 駢頗疑之，陰欲奪其權，而根蒂已固，無如之何。

translations.literal: Pian grew quite suspicious and secretly wished to seize back his power, but Yongzhi's roots were already firm and there was nothing to be done.
translations.idiomatic: Pian grew deeply suspicious and wanted secretly to claw back his authority, but Yongzhi's grip was already too deep to break.

sentences.zh: 用之知之，甚懼，訪於其黨前度支巡官鄭杞、前知廬州事董瑾，杞曰：「此固為晚矣！

translations.literal: Yongzhi learned of this and was greatly afraid. He consulted his faction members, former revenue circuit inspector Zheng Qi and former Luzhou administrator Dong Jin. Qi said: "This is already too late!
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi found out and was terrified. He turned to his allies, former revenue inspector Zheng Qi and former Luzhou administrator Dong Jin. Qi said: "It is already too late!

sentences.zh: 」用之問策安出，杞曰：「曹孟德有言：『寧我負人，無人負我。

translations.literal: Yongzhi asked where the plan would come from. Qi said: "Lord Cao had a saying: 'Better that I wrong others than that others wrong me.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi asked what plan Qi had in mind. Qi said: "Lord Cao once said: 'I would rather wrong others than let others wrong me.'

sentences.zh: 』」明日，與瑾共為書一緘授用之，其語秘，人莫有知者。

translations.literal: '"" The next day he and Jin jointly composed one sealed letter and gave it to Yongzhi; its words were secret, and no one knew them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he and Jin drafted a sealed letter and delivered it to Yongzhi; its contents were secret, and no one else knew what it said.

sentences.zh: 蕭遘稱疾歸永樂。

translations.literal: Xiao Xiong pleaded illness and returned to Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xiong pleaded illness and went home to Yongle.

sentences.zh: 初，鳳翔節度使李昌符與朱玫同謀立襄王，既而玫自為宰相專權，昌符怒，不受其官，更通表興元。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fengxiang military governor Li Changfu and Zhu Mei had jointly plotted to establish Prince Yun. Later Mei made himself chancellor and monopolized power. Changfu grew angry, refused his appointments, and instead sent memorials to Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Fengxiang governor Li Changfu and Zhu Mei had plotted together to put Prince Yun on the throne. When Mei took the chancellorship for himself and seized sole power, Changfu refused his appointments in anger and sent memorials instead to the court at Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 詔加昌符檢校司徒。

translations.literal: An edict added for Changfu the honorary post of situ.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Changfu honorary situ.

sentences.zh: 朱玫遣其將王行瑜將邠寧、河西兵五萬追乘輿，感義節度使楊晟戰數卻，棄散關走，行瑜進屯鳳州。

translations.literal: Zhu Mei dispatched his general Wang Xingyu to lead fifty thousand Bing-Ning and Hexi troops in pursuit of the imperial carriage. Ganyi military governor Yang Sheng fought several times and was driven back, abandoned Sanguan and fled, and Xingyu advanced to camp at Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei sent his general Wang Xingyu with fifty thousand Bing-Ning and Hexi troops to pursue the imperial carriage. Ganyi governor Yang Sheng fought several losing engagements, abandoned Sanguan Pass, and fled; Xingyu advanced and encamped at Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸道貢賦多之長安，不之興元，從官衛士皆乏食，上涕泣，不知為計。

translations.literal: At this time most circuit tribute and taxes went to Chang'an, not to Xingyuan. The attendant officials and guard troops all lacked food. The Emperor wept and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Most provincial tribute and tax receipts were going to Chang'an rather than Xingyuan. Attendants and imperial guards alike went hungry. The emperor wept, at a loss for what to do.

sentences.zh: 杜讓能言於上曰：「楊復光與王重榮同破黃巢，復京城，相親善；

translations.literal: Du Rangneng said to the Emperor: "Yang Fuguang and Wang Chongrong together defeated Huang Chao and recovered the capital; they are on close, friendly terms;
translations.idiomatic: Du Rangneng told the emperor: "Yang Fuguang and Wang Chongrong fought Huang Chao together and recovered the capital; they are on close terms;

sentences.zh: 復恭其兄也。

translations.literal: Fugong is his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong is his older brother.

sentences.zh: 若遣重臣往諭以大義，且致復恭之意，宜有回慮歸國之理。

translations.literal: If a high minister is sent to instruct him in the great principle and also convey Fugong's wishes, there ought to be reason for him to reconsider and return to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: If we send a senior minister to explain the court's cause and convey Fugong's message as well, he may well reconsider and return to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 」上從之，遣右諫議大夫劉崇望使於河中，繼詔諭重榮，重榮既聽命，遣使表獻絹十萬匹，且請討朱玫以自贖。

translations.literal: " The Emperor agreed, sent Right Remonstrance Grandee Liu Chongwang as envoy to Hezhong, and followed with an edict instructing Chongrong. Once Chongrong obeyed, he sent envoys with a memorial offering one hundred thousand bolts of silk and requesting to campaign against Zhu Mei to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent Right Remonstrance Grandee Liu Chongwang to Hezhong, followed by an edict instructing Chongrong. Chongrong accepted, sent envoys offering one hundred thousand bolts of silk, and asked to campaign against Zhu Mei to atone for himself.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，襄王熅遣使至晉陽賜李克用詔，言：「上至半塗，六軍變擾，蒼黃晏駕，吾為籓鎮所推，今已受冊。

translations.literal: On wuxu day Prince Yun of Xiang sent envoys to Jinyang bearing an edict for Li Keyong, stating: "The Emperor reached halfway when the Six Armies muttered and stirred; in sudden confusion he died untimely. I was pushed forward by the garrison commands and have now received investiture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day Prince Yun sent envoys to Jinyang with an edict for Li Keyong, saying: "The emperor was partway through the journey when the armies mutinied; in the panic he died untimely. The provinces pushed me forward, and I have now taken investiture.

sentences.zh: 」朱玫亦與克用書，克用聞其謀皆出於玫，大怒。

translations.literal: " Zhu Mei also wrote to Keyong. When Keyong learned the plot all came from Mei, he was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei also wrote to Keyong. Learning the whole plot came from Mei, Keyong flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 大將蓋寓說克用曰：「鑾輿播遷，天下皆歸咎於我，今不誅玫，黜李熅，無以自湔洗。

translations.literal: Major general Gai Yu urged Keyong, saying: "The imperial carriage has been driven into exile and the world blames us. If we do not execute Mei and remove Li Yun, we cannot wash ourselves clean.
translations.idiomatic: Major general Gai Yu urged Keyong: "The emperor has been driven into exile and the world blames us. Unless we execute Mei and remove Li Yun, we can never clear our name.

sentences.zh: 」克用從之，燔詔書，囚使者，移檄鄰道，稱：「玫敢欺籓方，明言晏駕。

translations.literal: " Keyong agreed. He burned the edict, imprisoned the envoys, and circulated a proclamation to neighboring circuits, stating: "Mei dares deceive the garrisons by openly declaring the Emperor's untimely death.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong agreed. He burned the edict, imprisoned the envoys, and issued a proclamation to neighboring circuits: "Mei dares deceive the provinces by openly announcing the emperor's untimely death.

sentences.zh: 當道已發蕃、漢三萬兵進討凶逆，當共立大功。

translations.literal: This circuit has already dispatched thirty thousand foreign and Chinese troops to campaign against the traitors. Let us together achieve great merit.
translations.idiomatic: This circuit has already dispatched thirty thousand foreign and Han troops against the traitors. Let us win glory together.

sentences.zh: 」寓，蔚州人也。

translations.literal: " Yu was a man of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 秦賢寇宋汴，朱全忠敗之於尉氏南；

translations.literal: Qin Xian raided Song and Bian. Zhu Quanzhong defeated him south of Weishi;
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xian raided Song and Bian. Zhu Quanzhong defeated him south of Weishi;

sentences.zh: 癸巳，遣都將郭言將步騎三萬擊蔡州。

translations.literal: On guisi day he dispatched commanding general Guo Yan to lead thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day he sent commanding general Guo Yan with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，以扈蹕都將楊守亮為金商節度、京畿制置使，將兵二萬出金州，與王重榮、李克用共討朱玫，守亮本姓訾，名亮，曹州人，與弟信皆為楊復光假子，更名守亮、守信。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Imperial Escort commanding general Yang Shouliang was made military governor of Jin-Shang and metropolitan commissioner for the capital region. He led twenty thousand troops out from Jin Prefecture to join Wang Chongrong and Li Keyong in campaigning against Zhu Mei. Shouliang's original surname was Zi, given name Liang; he was a man of Caozhou. He and his younger brother Xin were both Yang Fuguang's adopted sons and were renamed Shouliang and Shouxin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yang Shouliang, a commanding general of the imperial escort, was made governor of Jin-Shang and metropolitan commissioner for the capital region. He led twenty thousand men out of Jinzhou to join Wang Chongrong and Li Keyong against Zhu Mei. Shouliang, originally surnamed Zi with the given name Liang, was from Caozhou. He and his younger brother Xin were both adopted sons of Yang Fuguang and were renamed Shouliang and Shouxin.

sentences.zh: 李克用遣使奉表稱：「方發兵濟河，除逆黨，迎車駕，願詔諸道與臣協力。

translations.literal: Li Keyong sent envoys submitting a memorial stating: "I am just now dispatching troops to cross the river, eliminate the traitors, and welcome the imperial carriage. I ask that the circuits be ordered to cooperate with me.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent envoys with a memorial: "I am about to cross the river with troops to destroy the rebels and welcome the emperor back. I ask that the circuits be ordered to act with me.

sentences.zh: 」先是，山南之人皆言克用與朱玫合，人情忷懼；

translations.literal: " Earlier, the people of Shannan all said Keyong was in league with Zhu Mei, and public feeling was alarmed and fearful;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier people in Shannan had said Keyong was allied with Zhu Mei, and fear spread;

sentences.zh: 表至，上出示從官，並諭山南諸鎮，由是帖然。

translations.literal: when the memorial arrived the Emperor showed it to his attendants and also announced it to the Shannan garrisons, and thereby all grew calm.
translations.idiomatic: when the memorial arrived the emperor showed it to his attendants and announced it to the Shannan garrisons as well, and the alarm subsided.

sentences.zh: 然克用表猶以朱全忠為言，上使楊復恭以書諭之云：「俟三輔事寧，別有進止。

translations.literal: Yet Keyong's memorial still spoke of Zhu Quanzhong. The Emperor had Yang Fugong write to instruct him, saying: "Wait until affairs in the Three Metropolises are settled; then there will be separate orders.
translations.idiomatic: But Keyong's memorial still raised Zhu Quanzhong. The emperor had Yang Fugong write to him: "Wait until the Three Metropolises are pacified; further orders will follow.

sentences.zh: 衡州刺史周岳發兵攻潭州，欽化節度使閔勖招淮西將黃皓入城共守，皓遂殺勖。

translations.literal: Heng Prefecture prefect Zhou Yue raised troops to attack Tan Prefecture. Qinhua military governor Min Xu recruited Huaixi general Huang Hao into the city to hold it jointly, and Hao then killed Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Hengzhou prefect Zhou Yue raised troops to attack Tanzhou. Qinhua governor Min Xu brought Huaixi general Huang Hao into the city to help defend it, and Hao then killed Xu.

sentences.zh: 岳攻拔州城，擒皓，殺之。

translations.literal: Yue stormed and took the prefectural city, captured Hao, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue stormed the city, captured Hao, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 鎮海節度使周寶遣牙將丁從實襲常州，逐張郁。

translations.literal: Zhenhai military governor Zhou Bao dispatched staff general Ding Congshi to raid Chang Prefecture and drive out Zhang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenhai governor Zhou Bao sent staff general Ding Congshi to raid Changzhou and drive out Zhang Yu.

sentences.zh: 郁奔海陵，依鎮遏使南昌高霸。

translations.literal: Yu fled to Hailing and relied on suppression commissioner Gao Ba of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu fled to Hailing and took refuge with suppression commissioner Gao Ba of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 霸，高駢將也，鎮海陵，有民五萬戶，兵三萬人。

translations.literal: Ba was a general of Gao Pian; he held Hailing, with fifty thousand households and thirty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Ba was one of Gao Pian's generals. He held Hailing with fifty thousand households and thirty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，秦宗權陷許州，殺節度使鹿晏弘。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Qin Zongquan captured Xu Prefecture and killed military governor Lu Yanhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Qin Zongquan took Xuzhou and killed governor Lu Yanhong.

sentences.zh: 王行瑜進攻興州，感義節度使楊晟棄鎮走，據文州，詔保鑾都將李鋋、扈蹕都將李茂貞、陳佩屯大唐峰以拒之。

translations.literal: Wang Xingyu advanced to attack Xing Prefecture. Ganyi military governor Yang Sheng abandoned his post and fled, seized Wen Prefecture, and an edict ordered Imperial Guard commanding general Li Qian, Imperial Escort commanding general Li Maozhen, and Chen Pei to encamp at Datang Peak to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu advanced on Xingzhou. Ganyi governor Yang Sheng abandoned his post, fled, and seized Wenzhan; an edict ordered Imperial Guard commander Li Qian, Imperial Escort commander Li Maozhen, and Chen Pei to encamp at Datang Peak to block him.

sentences.zh: 茂貞，博野人，本姓宋，名文通，以功賜姓名。

translations.literal: Maozhen was a man of Boye; his original surname was Song and given name Wentong; for merit he was granted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen was from Boye; his original surname was Song and given name Wentong; for merit he was granted the name Maozhen.

sentences.zh: 要命欽化軍曰武安，以衡州刺史周岳為節度使。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that the Qinhua army be renamed Wu'an, and Heng Prefecture prefect Zhou Yue was made its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed the Qinhua army Wu'an and made Hengzhou prefect Zhou Yue its military governor.

sentences.zh: 八月，盧龍節度使李全忠薨，以其子匡威為留後。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Lulong military governor Li Quanzhong died; his son Kuangwei was made acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Lulong governor Li Quanzhong died; his son Kuangwei was made acting governor.

sentences.zh: 王潮拔泉州，殺廖彥若。

translations.literal: Wang Chao captured Quan Prefecture and killed Liao Yanruo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chao took Quanzhou and killed Liao Yanruo.

sentences.zh: 潮聞福建觀察陳巖威名，不敢犯福州境，遣使降之，巖表潮為泉州刺史。

translations.literal: Chao heard of the renown of Fujian observation commissioner Chen Yan and did not dare invade Fuzhou territory. He sent envoys to submit, and Yan memorialized that Chao be made prefect of Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Fujian observer Chen Yan's reputation, Chao did not dare cross into Fuzhou. He sent envoys to submit, and Yan memorialized to make him prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 潮沈勇有智略，既得泉州，招懷離散，均賦繕兵，吏民悅服。

translations.literal: Chao was deep, brave, and resourceful. Once he held Quan Prefecture, he gathered in the scattered, equalized taxes, repaired arms, and officials and people were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Deep, brave, and shrewd, Chao once he held Quanzhou gathered in the scattered population, equalized taxes, repaired arms, and won over officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 幽王緒於別館，緒慚，自殺。

translations.literal: He kept You Prince Xu at a separate lodge; Xu was ashamed and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He kept You Prince Xu at a separate lodge; ashamed, Xu killed himself.

sentences.zh: 九月，朱玫將張行實攻大唐峰，李鋋等擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Zhu Mei's general Zhang Xingshi attacked Datang Peak, and Li Qian and the others drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Zhu Mei's general Zhang Xingshi attacked Datang Peak; Li Qian and the others beat him back.

sentences.zh: 金吾將軍滿存與邠軍戰，破之，復取興州，進守萬仞寨。

translations.literal: Gold Crow general Man Cun fought the Bing troops, defeated them, recovered Xing Prefecture, and advanced to hold Wanyren Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Gold Crow general Man Cun fought the Bing army, defeated it, recovered Xingzhou, and advanced to hold Wanyren Fort.

sentences.zh: 李克修攻孟方立，甲午，擒其將呂臻於焦岡，拔故鎮、武安、臨洺、邯鄲、沙河，以大將安金俊為邢州刺史。

translations.literal: Li Kexiu attacked Meng Fangli. On jiawu day he captured Fangli's general Lu Zhen at Jiaogang, took Gu Town, Wu'an, Linming, Handan, and Shahe, and made major general An Jinjun prefect of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kexiu attacked Meng Fangli. On jiawu day he captured Fangli's general Lu Zhen at Jiaogang, took Gu Town, Wu'an, Linming, Handan, and Shahe, and made major general An Jinjun prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 長安百官太子太師裴璩等勸進於襄王熅。

translations.literal: The Chang'an officials led by Junior Tutor to the Heir Pei Su urged Prince Yun to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an officials led by junior tutor to the heir Pei Su urged Prince Yun to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，熅即皇帝位，改元建貞，遙尊上為太上元皇帝。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Yun assumed the imperial throne, changed the era name to Jianzhen, and honored the Emperor from afar as Supreme Primordial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Yun took the throne, changed the era name to Jianzhen, and honored the emperor from afar as Supreme Primordial Emperor.

sentences.zh: 董昌謂錢鏐曰：「汝能取越州，吾以杭州授汝。

translations.literal: Dong Chang said to Qian Liu: "If you can take Yue Prefecture, I will give you Hang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chang told Qian Liu: "If you can take Yuezhou, I will give you Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 」鏐曰：「然，不取終為後患。

translations.literal: " Liu said: "Yes—and if we do not take it, it will be a trouble later.
translations.idiomatic: Liu replied: "Agreed. If we leave it untaken, it will trouble us later.

sentences.zh: 」遂將兵自諸暨趨平水，鑿山開道五百里，出曹娥埭，浙東將鮑君福帥眾降之。

translations.literal: " He then led troops from Zhuji toward Pingshui, cut through mountains and opened a road five hundred li, emerged at Cao'e Embankment, and Zhedong general Bao Junfu led his forces to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He then led troops from Zhuji toward Pingshui, cut a road five hundred li through the mountains, emerged at Cao'e Embankment, and Zhedong general Bao Junfu submitted with his forces.

sentences.zh: 鏐與浙東軍戰，屢破之，進屯豐山。

translations.literal: Liu fought the Zhedong army, repeatedly defeated it, and advanced to encamp at Feng Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu fought the Zhedong army, defeated it repeatedly, and advanced to encamp at Feng Mountain.

sentences.zh: 感化牙將張雄、馮弘鐸得罪於節度使時溥，聚眾三百，走渡江，襲蘇州，據之。

translations.literal: Ganhu staff generals Zhang Xiong and Feng Hongduo offended military governor Shi Pu, gathered three hundred men, fled across the river, raided Su Prefecture, and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Ganhu staff generals Zhang Xiong and Feng Hongduo offended governor Shi Pu, gathered three hundred men, fled across the river, raided Suzhou, and seized it.

sentences.zh: 雄自稱刺史，稍聚兵至五萬，戰艦千餘，自號天成軍。

translations.literal: Xiong styled himself prefect, gradually gathered troops to fifty thousand, more than a thousand warships, and called his force the Tiancheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong styled himself prefect, gradually built his force to fifty thousand men and more than a thousand warships, and called his army the Tiancheng Army.

sentences.zh: 河陽節度使諸葛爽薨，大將劉經、張全義立爽子仲方為留後。

translations.literal: Heyang military governor Zhuge Shuang died; major generals Liu Jing and Zhang Quanyi installed Shuang's son Zhongfang as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang governor Zhuge Shuang died; major generals Liu Jing and Zhang Quanyi installed Shuang's son Zhongfang as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 全義，臨濮人也。

translations.literal: Quanyi was a man of Linpu.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi was from Linpu.

sentences.zh: 李克修攻邢州，不克而還。

translations.literal: Li Kexiu attacked Xing Prefecture, failed to take it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kexiu attacked Xingzhou, failed to take it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙戌，錢鏐克越州，劉漢宏奔台州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on bingxu day, Qian Liu captured Yue Prefecture; Liu Hanhong fled to Tai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingxu day, Qian Liu captured Yuezhou; Liu Hanhong fled to Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 義成節度使安師儒委政於兩廂都虞候夏侯晏、杜標，二人驕恣，軍中忿之。

translations.literal: Yicheng military governor An Shiru entrusted government to the two wing chief military adjutants Xia Houyan and Du Biao. The two were arrogant and willful, and the army resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng governor An Shiru left government to his two wing chief military adjutants Xia Houyan and Du Biao. The two grew arrogant and willful, and the army resented them.

sentences.zh: 小校張驍潛出，聚眾二千攻州城，師儒斬晏、標首諭之，軍中稍息。

translations.literal: Junior officer Zhang Xiao slipped out secretly, gathered two thousand men, and attacked the prefectural city. Shiru beheaded Yan and Biao and displayed their heads to explain, and the army gradually calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Junior officer Zhang Xiao slipped out, gathered two thousand men, and attacked the city. Shiru beheaded Yan and Biao and displayed their heads to the troops, and the unrest gradually subsided.

sentences.zh: 天平節度使朱瑄謀取滑州，遣濮州刺史朱裕將兵誘張驍，殺之。

translations.literal: Tianping military governor Zhu Xuan plotted to take Hua Prefecture and dispatched Pu Prefecture prefect Zhu Yu to lead troops and lure Zhang Xiao and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianping governor Zhu Xuan plotted to take Huazhou and sent Pu prefect Zhu Yu with troops to lure Zhang Xiao and kill him.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠先遣其將朱珍、李唐賓襲滑州，入境，遇大雪。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong first dispatched his generals Zhu Zhen and Li Tangbin to raid Hua Prefecture. They entered the territory and encountered heavy snow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong first sent his generals Zhu Zhen and Li Tangbin to raid Huazhou. They entered the territory and ran into heavy snow.

sentences.zh: 珍等一夕馳至壁下，百梯並升，遂克之。

translations.literal: Zhen and the others galloped in one night to the foot of the wall; a hundred ladders rose together, and they took it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and the others rode through the night to the foot of the wall; a hundred ladders went up at once, and they took the city.

sentences.zh: 虜師儒以歸。

translations.literal: They captured Shiru and took him back.
translations.idiomatic: They captured Shiru and took him away.

sentences.zh: 全忠以牙將江陵胡真知義成留後。

translations.literal: Quanzhong made staff general Hu Zhen of Jiangling acting governor of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong made Jiangling staff general Hu Zhen acting governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 田令孜至成都請尋醫，許之。

translations.literal: Tian Lingci reached Chengdu and requested leave to seek medical treatment; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingci reached Chengdu and asked leave to seek medical treatment; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊寅，諸軍拔鳳州，以滿存為鳳州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuyin day, the various armies captured Feng Prefecture, and Man Cun was made defense commissioner of Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuyin day, the allied armies took Fengzhou, and Man Cun was made defense commissioner of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊復恭傳檄關中，稱「得朱玫首者，以靜難節度使賞之。

translations.literal: Yang Fugong circulated a proclamation in Guanzhong, stating: "Whoever obtains Zhu Mei's head will be rewarded with the post of Jingnan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fugong circulated a proclamation in Guanzhong: "Whoever brings in Zhu Mei's head will receive the post of Jingnan military governor.

sentences.zh: 」王行瑜戰數敗，恐獲罪於玫，與其下謀曰：「今無功，歸亦死；

translations.literal: " Wang Xingyu had been defeated repeatedly in battle and feared punishment from Mei. He consulted his subordinates, saying: "Now with no achievement, if we return we will also die;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu had lost battle after battle and feared punishment from Mei. He consulted his men: "With nothing accomplished, we die even if we go back;

sentences.zh: 曷若與汝曹斬玫首，定京城，迎大駕，取邠寧節鉞乎？

translations.literal: why not with you all cut off Mei's head, pacify the capital, welcome the great carriage, and take the Bing-Ning command?
translations.idiomatic: why not cut off Mei's head, pacify the capital, welcome the emperor back, and win the Bing-Ning command?

sentences.zh: 」眾從之。

translations.literal: " The crowd agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The men agreed.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，行瑜自鳳州擅兵引歸京師，玫方視事，聞之，怒，召行諭，責之曰：「汝擅歸，欲反邪？

translations.literal: On jiayin day Xingyu led his troops without authorization from Feng Prefecture back to the capital. Mei was just conducting business when he heard this, grew angry, summoned Xingyu, and rebuked him: "You returned without leave—do you mean to rebel?
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day Xingyu marched his troops without authorization from Fengzhou back to the capital. Mei was at his desk when he heard of it, flew into a rage, summoned Xingyu, and rebuked him: "You returned without leave—do you mean to rebel?

sentences.zh: 」行瑜曰：「吾不反，欲誅反者朱玫耳！

translations.literal: " Xingyu said: "I do not rebel—I mean to execute the rebel Zhu Mei!
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu said: "I am not rebelling—I mean to execute the rebel Zhu Mei!

sentences.zh: 」遂擒斬之，並殺其黨數百人。

translations.literal: " He then seized and beheaded him, and also killed several hundred of his faction.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized Mei and beheaded him, and killed several hundred of his followers as well.

sentences.zh: 諸軍大亂，焚掠京城，士民無衣凍死者蔽地。

translations.literal: The various armies fell into great disorder, burned and plundered the capital, and commoners without clothing who froze to death covered the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The armies fell into chaos, burned and plundered the capital, and the ground was covered with commoners who had no clothes and froze to death.

sentences.zh: 裴澈、鄭昌圖帥百官二百餘人奉襄王奔河中，王重榮詐為迎奉，執熅，殺之，囚澈、昌圖；

translations.literal: Pei Che and Zheng Changtu led more than two hundred officials escorting Prince Yun in flight to Hezhong. Wang Chongrong pretended to welcome them, seized Yun, killed him, and imprisoned Che and Changtu;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Che and Zheng Changtu led more than two hundred officials escorting Prince Yun in flight to Hezhong. Wang Chongrong feigned a welcome, seized Yun, killed him, and imprisoned Che and Changtu;

sentences.zh: 百官死者殆半。

translations.literal: nearly half the officials died.
translations.idiomatic: nearly half the officials died.

sentences.zh: 台州刺史杜雄誘劉漢宏，執送董昌，斬之。

translations.literal: Tai Prefecture prefect Du Xiong lured Liu Hanhong, seized him, sent him to Dong Chang, and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou prefect Du Xiong lured Liu Hanhong, seized him, sent him to Dong Chang, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 昌徙鎮越州，自稱知浙東軍府事，以錢鏐知杭州事。

translations.literal: Chang moved his seat of command to Yue Prefecture, styled himself administrator of the Zhedong military prefecture, and made Qian Liu administrator of Hang Prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chang moved his headquarters to Yuezhou, styled himself administrator of the Zhedong military prefecture, and made Qian Liu administrator of Hangzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 王重榮函襄王熅首送行在，刑部請御興元城南門獻馘，百官畢賀。

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong sent Prince Yun's head in a box to the temporary court. The Ministry of Punishments requested that at the south gate of Xingyuan the head be presented as a trophy before the Emperor, and all officials congratulate in full.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong sent Prince Yun's head in a box to the temporary court. The Ministry of Punishments asked that the head be presented as a trophy before the emperor at Xingyuan's south gate and that all officials congratulate.

sentences.zh: 太常博士殷盈孫議，以為：「熅為賊臣所逼，正以不能死節罪耳。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun argued, saying: "Yun was compelled by traitorous ministers; his fault lay only in failing to die for principle.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun argued: "Yun was forced by traitorous ministers; his only fault was failing to die for principle.

sentences.zh: 禮，公族罪在大辟，君為之素服不舉。

translations.literal: By ritual, when a member of the ducal clan is guilty of capital crime, the ruler wears unadorned mourning and suspends music.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual, when a member of the imperial clan is guilty of a capital crime, the ruler wears plain mourning and suspends music.

sentences.zh: 今熅已就誅，宜廢為庶人，令所在葬其首。

translations.literal: Now that Yun has already been executed, he should be degraded to commoner status and his head buried wherever it may be.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Yun has been executed, he should be degraded to commoner status and his head buried wherever it lies.

sentences.zh: 其獻馘稱賀之禮，請俟朱玫首至而行之。

translations.literal: As for the rites of presenting trophies and offering congratulations, please wait until Zhu Mei's head arrives before performing them.
translations.idiomatic: The rites of presenting trophies and offering congratulations should wait until Zhu Mei's head arrives.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 盈孫，侑之孫也。

translations.literal: Yingsun was a grandson of You.
translations.idiomatic: Yingsun was a grandson of You.

sentences.zh: 河陽大將劉經，畏李罕之難制，自引兵鎮洛陽，襲罕之於澠池，為罕之所敗，經棄洛陽走，罕之追殺殆盡。

translations.literal: Heyang major general Liu Jing, fearing Li Hanzhi would be hard to control, himself led troops to hold Luoyang and raided Hanzhi at Mianchi. He was defeated by Hanzhi; Jing abandoned Luoyang and fled, and Hanzhi pursued and killed nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang major general Liu Jing, fearing Li Hanzhi would be hard to control, led troops to hold Luoyang and raided Hanzhi at Mianchi. Hanzhi defeated him; Jing abandoned Luoyang and fled, and Hanzhi pursued and killed nearly all his men.

sentences.zh: 罕之軍於鞏，將渡河，經遣張全義將兵拒之。

translations.literal: Hanzhi encamped at Gong and was about to cross the river. Jing dispatched Zhang Quanyi to lead troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi encamped at Gong and prepared to cross the river. Jing sent Zhang Quanyi with troops to block him.

sentences.zh: 時諸葛仲方幼弱，政在劉經，諸將多不附。

translations.literal: At the time Zhuge Zhongfang was young and weak; government lay with Liu Jing, and most generals did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Zhongfang was still young; power lay with Liu Jing, and most generals would not follow him.

sentences.zh: 全義遂與罕之合兵攻河陽，為經所敗，罕之、全義走保懷州。

translations.literal: Quanyi then joined forces with Hanzhi to attack Heyang, was defeated by Jing, and Hanzhi and Quanyi fled to hold Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi then joined Hanzhi to attack Heyang, was defeated by Jing, and Hanzhi and Quanyi fled to hold Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，忠武決勝指揮使孫儒與龍驤指揮使朗山劉建鋒戍蔡州，拒黃巢，扶溝馬殷隸軍中，以材勇聞。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhongwu Decisive Victory commanding general Sun Ru and Dragon Courage commanding general Liu Jianfeng of Langshan garrisoned Cai Prefecture to resist Huang Chao. Fugou's Ma Yin served in the army and was known for talent and bravery.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhongwu Decisive Victory commander Sun Ru and Dragon Courage commander Liu Jianfeng of Langshan garrisoned Caizhou against Huang Chao. Fugou's Ma Yin served in the army and was known for talent and bravery.

sentences.zh: 及秦宗權叛，儒等皆屬焉。

translations.literal: When Qin Zongquan rebelled, Ru and the others all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Zongquan rebelled, Ru and the others all joined him.

sentences.zh: 宗權遣儒將兵攻陷鄭州，刺史李璠奔大梁。

translations.literal: Zongquan dispatched Ru to lead troops, attack and capture Zheng Prefecture; prefect Li Fan fled to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Zongquan sent Ru to attack and capture Zhengzhou; prefect Li Fan fled to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 儒進陷河陽，留後諸葛仲方奔大梁。

translations.literal: Ru advanced and captured Heyang; acting governor Zhuge Zhongfang fled to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Ru advanced and took Heyang; acting governor Zhuge Zhongfang fled to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 儒自稱節度使，張全義據懷州，李罕之據澤州以拒之。

translations.literal: Ru styled himself military governor. Zhang Quanyi held Huai Prefecture and Li Hanzhi held Ze Prefecture to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Ru styled himself military governor. Zhang Quanyi held Huaizhou and Li Hanzhi held Zezhou to resist him.

sentences.zh: 初，長安人張佶為宣州幕僚，惡觀察使秦彥之為人，棄官去，過蔡州，宗權留以為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chang'an man Zhang Ji was a staff member in Xuan Prefecture. Disliking the character of observation commissioner Qin Yan, he abandoned his post and left. Passing through Cai Prefecture, Zongquan retained him as campaign marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chang'an native Zhang Ji had been on the staff in Xuanzhou. Disliking observer Qin Yan's character, he quit his post. Passing through Caizhou, Zongquan kept him as campaign marshal.

sentences.zh: 佶謂劉建鋒曰：「秦公剛鷙而猜忌，亡無日矣，吾屬何以自免！

translations.literal: Ji said to Liu Jianfeng: "Lord Qin is stern and fierce yet suspicious; his fall will come any day. How are we to save ourselves!
translations.idiomatic: Ji told Liu Jianfeng: "Lord Qin is harsh, fierce, and suspicious; he will fall any day. How are we to save ourselves?

sentences.zh: 」建鋒方自危，遂與佶善。

translations.literal: " Jianfeng was himself in peril and therefore became friendly with Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng was already in peril and therefore became close with Ji.

sentences.zh: 壽州刺史張翱遣其將魏虔將萬人寇廬州，廬州刺史楊行愍遣其將田頵、李神福、張訓拒之，敗虔於褚城。

translations.literal: Shou Prefecture prefect Zhang Ao dispatched his general Wei Qian to lead ten thousand men to raid Lu Prefecture. Lu Prefecture prefect Yang Xingmin dispatched his generals Tian Jun, Li Shenfu, and Zhang Xun to resist them and defeated Qian at Zhucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhou prefect Zhang Ao sent his general Wei Qian with ten thousand men to raid Luzhou. Luzhou prefect Yang Xingmin sent his generals Tian Jun, Li Shenfu, and Zhang Xun to resist and defeated Qian at Zhucheng.

sentences.zh: 滁州刺史許勍襲舒州，刺史陶雅奔廬州。

translations.literal: Chu Prefecture prefect Xu Qing raided Shu Prefecture; prefect Tao Ya fled to Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou prefect Xu Qing raided Shuzhou; prefect Tao Ya fled to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 高駢命行愍更名行密。

translations.literal: Gao Pian ordered Xingmin to change his name to Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian ordered Xingmin to change his name to Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天平牙將朱瑾逐泰寧節度使齊克讓，自稱留後。

translations.literal: That year, Tianping staff general Zhu Jin drove out Taining military governor Qi Kerang and styled himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tianping staff general Zhu Jin drove out Taining governor Qi Kerang and styled himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 瑾將襲袞州，求婚於克讓，乃自鄆盛飾車服，私藏兵甲以赴之。

translations.literal: Jin was about to raid Yan Prefecture. He sought Kerang's daughter in marriage, then from Yan grandly adorned chariots and robes and secretly concealed arms and armor when he went to the wedding.
translations.idiomatic: Jin planned to raid Yanzhou. He sought Kerang's daughter in marriage, then from Yan set out in grand chariots and robes with arms and armor hidden beneath.

sentences.zh: 親迎之夕，甲士竊發，逐克讓而代之。

translations.literal: On the night of welcoming the bride, armored men sprang up in secret, drove out Kerang, and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding night armored men sprang up, drove out Kerang, and replaced him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因以瑾為泰寧節度使。

translations.literal: The court thereupon appointed Jin military governor of Taining.
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon confirmed Jin as military governor of Taining.

sentences.zh: 安陸賊帥周通攻鄂州，路審中亡去。

translations.literal: Anlu bandit chieftain Zhou Tong attacked E Prefecture; Lu Shenzhong fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tong, a rebel leader from Anlu, attacked Ezhou; Lu Shenzhong fled.

sentences.zh: 岳州刺史杜洪乘虛入鄂，自稱武昌留後，朝廷因以授之。

translations.literal: Yue Prefecture prefect Du Hong seized the opportunity to enter E, styled himself acting governor of Wuchang, and the court thereupon invested him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong, prefect of Yuezhou, slipped into Ezhou while it was undefended, styled himself acting governor of Wuchang, and the court confirmed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 湘陰賊帥鄧進思復乘虛陷岳州。

translations.literal: Xiangyin bandit chieftain Deng Jinshi again seized the opportunity and took Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jinshi, a rebel leader from Xiangyin, again seized the moment and captured Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 秦宗言圍荊南二年，張瑰嬰城自守，城中米斗直錢四十緡，食甲鼓皆盡，擊門扉以警夜，死者相枕。

translations.literal: Qin Zongyan besieged Jingnan for two years. Zhang Gui held the city and defended himself. In the city a dou of rice cost forty strings of cash; food, armor, and drums were all exhausted; they struck door panels to keep watch at night; the dead lay piled upon each other.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongyan besieged Jingnan for two years. Zhang Gui barricaded himself inside the walls. Rice in the city sold for forty strings of cash per dou; food, armor, and drums were all used up; at night they beat door panels in lieu of watch drums; corpses lay stacked one upon another.

sentences.zh: 宗言竟不能克而去。

translations.literal: Zongyan in the end could not capture it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Zongyan failed to take the city and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 僖宗惠聖恭定孝皇帝下之上光啟三年（

translations.literal: Below [the account of] Emperor Xizong Huisheng Gongding Xiaoxiao, Part One: Guangqi year 3 (
translations.idiomatic: Below [the account of] Emperor Xizong, Huisheng Gongding Xiaoxiao, Part One—Guangqi year 3 (

sentences.zh: 丁未，公元八八七年）

translations.literal: Dingwei, equivalent to 887 CE)
translations.idiomatic: Dingwei, equivalent to 887 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，以邠州都將王行瑜為靜難軍節度使，扈蹕都頭李茂貞領武定節度使，扈蹕都頭楊守宗為金商節度使，右衛大將軍顧彥朗為東川節度使，金商節度使楊守亮為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Binzhou garrison commander Wang Xingyu was made military governor of the Jingnan Army; imperial escort commander Li Maozhen took charge as military governor of Wuding; imperial escort commander Yang Shouzong was made military governor of Jin and Shang; Right Guard great general Gu Yanslang was made military governor of Dongchuan; and Jin-Shang military governor Yang Shouliang was made military governor of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Wang Xingyu, garrison commander of Binzhou, was appointed military governor of Jingnan; Li Maozhen, head of the imperial escort, was put in charge of Wuding; Yang Shouzong, also of the escort guard, was made governor of Jin and Shang; Gu Yanslang, great general of the Right Guard, was made governor of Dongchuan; and Yang Shouliang, governor of Jin-Shang, was transferred to Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 彥朗，豐縣人也。

translations.literal: Yanslang was a man of Feng County.
translations.idiomatic: Yanslang was from Feng County.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以董昌為浙東觀察使，錢鏐為杭州刺史。

translations.literal: On xinsi day, Dong Chang was made observation commissioner of Zhedong, and Qian Liu was made prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day, Dong Chang was appointed observation commissioner of Zhedong and Qian Liu prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權自以兵力十倍於朱全忠，而數為全忠所敗，恥之，欲悉力以攻汴州。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan considered his forces ten times those of Zhu Quanzhong, yet he had repeatedly been defeated by Quanzhong; shamed, he wished to commit his full strength to attacking Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan believed his army outnumbered Zhu Quanzhong's tenfold, yet Quanzhong had beaten him again and again. Stung by the shame, he resolved to throw his full strength against Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 全忠患兵少，二月，以諸軍都指揮使朱珍為淄州刺史，募兵於東道，期以初夏而還。

translations.literal: Quanzhong worried his troops were too few; in the second month he made Combined Armies commander-in-chief Zhu Zhen prefect of Zi Prefecture to recruit troops in the eastern circuit, with a fixed date to return in early summer.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong worried that his forces were too thin. In the second month he made Zhu Zhen, overall commander of all armies, prefect of Zibo and sent him to recruit troops in the eastern circuits, with orders to return by early summer.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，削奪三川都監田令孜官爵，長流端州。

translations.literal: On wuchen day, the rank and titles of Three Circuits overseer Tian Lingzi were stripped, and he was banished far to Duan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day the court stripped Tian Lingzi, overseer of the Three Circuits, of rank and title and banished him to distant Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 然令孜依陳敬瑄，竟不行。

translations.literal: Yet Lingzi relied on Chen Jingxuan, and in the end the order was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: But Lingzi had Chen Jingxuan's protection, and in the end the exile was never enforced.

sentences.zh: 代北節度使李國昌薨。

translations.literal: Daibei military governor Li Guochang died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guochang, military governor of Daibei, died.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸未，詔偽宰相蕭遘、鄭昌圖、裴澈，於所在集眾斬之，皆死於岐山。

translations.literal: In the third month, on guiwei day, an edict [ordered that] the false chancellors Xiao Kui, Zheng Changtu, and Pei Che be publicly beheaded wherever found; all died at Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guiwei day, the court decreed that the renegade chancellors Xiao Kui, Zheng Changtu, and Pei Che were to be executed before assembled crowds wherever caught; all three died at Qishan.

sentences.zh: 時朝士受熅官者甚眾，法司皆處以極法。

translations.literal: At the time very many court officials had accepted offices from Chao; the legal authorities all sentenced them to the ultimate penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Many court officials had accepted posts from Huang Chao's regime; the judicial authorities were recommending the death penalty for all of them.

sentences.zh: 杜讓能力爭之，免者什七八。

translations.literal: Du Rangneng argued strenuously against this; seven or eight tenths were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Du Rangneng argued forcefully on their behalf; seven or eight out of ten were spared.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，車駕至鳳翔，節度使李昌符，恐車駕還京雖不治前過，恩賞必疏，乃以宮室未完，固請駐驊府捨，從之。

translations.literal: On renchen day, the imperial carriage reached Fengxiang. Military governor Li Changfu, fearing that even if the carriage returned to the capital his past faults would go unpunished but rewards and favor would surely be sparse, therefore cited unfinished palace halls and firmly requested that it remain at the Huafu lodging; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day the emperor reached Fengxiang. Li Changfu, military governor there, feared that even if the court returned to Chang'an his old misconduct would be overlooked while fresh rewards passed him by. He pleaded that the palace buildings were still incomplete and insisted the emperor stay at the Huafu lodge; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 太傅兼侍中鄭從讜罷為太子太保。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor and concurrently Palace Secretary Zheng Congdang was removed and made Crown Prince Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Congdang was demoted from Grand Preceptor and Palace Secretary to Crown Prince Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 鎮海節度使周寶募親軍千人，號後樓兵，稟給倍於鎮海軍，鎮海軍皆怨，而後樓兵浸驕不可制。

translations.literal: Zhenhai military governor Zhou Bao recruited a thousand personal troops, styled them the Rear Pavilion Army; their rations were double those of the Zhenhai Army; the Zhenhai Army all resented this, while the Rear Pavilion troops grew increasingly arrogant and uncontrollable.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bao, military governor of Zhenhai, recruited a thousand personal guards, called the Rear Pavilion Army, and paid them double what the regular Zhenhai troops received. The Zhenhai Army seethed with resentment, while the Rear Pavilion guards grew ever more arrogant and unruly.

sentences.zh: 寶溺於聲色，不親政事，築羅城二十餘里，建東第，人苦其役。

translations.literal: Bao drowned himself in music and women and did not attend to governance; he built outer walls more than twenty li long and erected an eastern mansion; people suffered under the corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: Bao drowned himself in pleasure and neglected affairs of state. He built more than twenty li of outer walls and an eastern mansion; the people groaned under the forced labor.

sentences.zh: 寶與僚屬宴後樓，有言鎮海軍怨望者，寶曰：「亂則殺之！

translations.literal: Bao feasted with his staff on the rear pavilion. When someone spoke of resentment among the Zhenhai Army, Bao said: "If they rebel, kill them!
translations.idiomatic: While feasting with his officials in the rear pavilion, Bao heard that the Zhenhai Army was muttering in discontent. He said: "If they rise up, kill them!

sentences.zh: 」度支催勤使薛朗以其言告所善鎮海軍將劉浩，戒之使戢士卒，浩曰：「惟反可以免死耳！

translations.literal: " Revenue and corvée mobilization envoy Xue Lang relayed these words to Liu Hao, a Zhenhai Army general with whom he was close, and warned him to restrain the soldiers. Hao said: "Only rebellion can spare one from death!
translations.idiomatic: " Xue Lang, corvée mobilization envoy of the revenue bureau, repeated this to his friend Liu Hao, a Zhenhai Army general, and urged him to keep the troops in check. Hao said: "Rebellion is the only way to escape death!

sentences.zh: 」是夕，寶醉，方寢，浩帥其黨作亂，攻府捨而焚之。

translations.literal: " That same night, Bao was drunk and had just gone to bed when Hao led his faction in revolt, attacked the headquarters, and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: " That night Bao was drunk and asleep when Hao led his men in revolt, stormed the headquarters, and burned it down.

sentences.zh: 寶驚起，徒跣叩芙蓉門呼後樓兵，後樓兵亦反矣。

translations.literal: Bao started up in alarm, ran barefoot to knock at Furong Gate and call the Rear Pavilion Army—the Rear Pavilion troops rebelled as well.
translations.idiomatic: Bao bolted awake and ran barefoot to Furong Gate to summon the Rear Pavilion guards—they had turned against him too.

sentences.zh: 寶帥家人步走出青陽門，遂奔常州，依刺史丁從實。

translations.literal: Bao led his family on foot out through Qingyang Gate, then fled to Chang Prefecture and placed himself under Prefect Ding Congshi.
translations.idiomatic: Bao fled on foot with his family through Qingyang Gate, made for Changzhou, and threw himself on the mercy of Prefect Ding Congshi.

sentences.zh: 浩殺諸僚佐，癸巳，迎薛朗入府，推為留後。

translations.literal: Hao killed the various staff officers; on guisi day he welcomed Xue Lang into headquarters and installed him as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Hao slaughtered Bao's staff. On guisi day he brought Xue Lang into headquarters and installed him as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 寶先兼租庸副使，城中貨財山積，是日，盡於亂兵之手。

translations.literal: Bao had earlier also held the concurrent post of deputy commissioner for land tax and labor levies; goods and wealth in the city were piled mountain-high; on that day, all fell to the mutineers.
