translations.idiomatic: Bao had also served as deputy commissioner for land tax and corvée; the city's wealth had been piled high—on that day the mutineers seized it all.

sentences.zh: 高駢聞寶敗，列牙受賀，遣使饋以齏粉。

translations.literal: Gao Pian heard that Bao had been defeated; he held a formal levee to receive congratulations and sent envoys presenting salted vegetables and flour.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Pian heard of Bao's defeat, he held a ceremonial review to celebrate and sent envoys bearing gifts of pickled vegetables and flour—a gibe at Bao's ruin.

sentences.zh: 寶怒，擲之地曰：「汝有呂用之在，他日未可知也！

translations.literal: Bao was enraged, threw them to the ground, and said: "You still have Lu Yongzhi in your service—what may come of you one day is not yet known!
translations.idiomatic: Bao flung the gifts to the ground in a rage and said: "As long as you keep Lu Yongzhi at your side, your own day may yet come!

sentences.zh: 」揚州連歲饑，城中餒死者日數千人，坊巷為之寥落，妖異數見，駢悉以為周寶當之。

translations.literal: " Yangzhou had suffered famine for successive years; each day several thousand starved to death in the city; lanes and wards grew desolate; strange portents appeared repeatedly; Pian ascribed them all to Zhou Bao as cause.
translations.idiomatic: " Yangzhou had famine year after year; thousands starved to death in the city each day; streets emptied; omens multiplied—and Pian blamed every one of them on Zhou Bao.

sentences.zh: 山南西道節度使楊守亮忌利州刺史王建驍勇，屢召之。

translations.literal: Shannan West Circuit military governor Yang Shouliang envied Lizhou prefect Wang Jian's valor and repeatedly summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shouliang, governor of Shannan West Circuit, envied Wang Jian, prefect of Lizhou, for his fighting prowess and summoned him again and again.

sentences.zh: 建懼，不往。

translations.literal: Jian feared and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was afraid and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 前龍州司倉周庠說建曰：「唐祚將終，籓鎮互相吞噬，皆無雄才遠略，不能戡濟多難。

translations.literal: Former Longzhou revenue clerk Zhou Xiang urged Jian, saying: "The Tang mandate is nearing its end; the garrisons devour one another; none has heroic talent or far-reaching design, and none can quell these many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xiang, a former revenue clerk from Longzhou, advised Jian: "The Tang dynasty is dying. The regional garrisons are tearing one another apart, and none of their leaders has the vision or ability to end the chaos.

sentences.zh: 公勇而有謀，得士卒心，立大功者非公而誰！

translations.literal: You, sir, are brave and resourceful and hold the hearts of the soldiers—who but you can achieve great merit!
translations.idiomatic: You are brave and shrewd, and your men follow you willingly. If anyone can win great glory, it is you!

sentences.zh: 然葭萌四戰之地，難以久安。

translations.literal: Yet Jimeng is a place fought over from all four directions; it is hard to hold secure for long.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jimeng lies at a crossroads of contending armies; you cannot hold it for long.

sentences.zh: 閬州地僻人富，楊茂實，陳、田之腹心，不修職貢，若表其罪，興兵討之，可一戰而擒也。

translations.literal: Lang Prefecture is remote and its people wealthy. Yang Maoshi is a trusted confidant of Chen and Tian; he does not maintain tribute to the court. If you memorialize his crimes and raise troops to punish him, he can be captured in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: Langzhou is remote and rich. Its prefect Yang Maoshi is a creature of Chen Jingxuan and Tian Lingzi and pays no tribute to the court. Denounce his crimes and march against him—you can take him in one battle.

sentences.zh: 」建從之，召募溪洞酋豪，有眾八千，沿嘉陵江而下，襲閬州，逐其刺史楊茂實而據之，自稱防禦使，招納亡命，軍勢益盛，守亮不能制。

translations.literal: " Jian followed this advice, recruited chieftains of stream valleys and cave settlements, mustered eight thousand men, descended along the Jialing River, raided Lang Prefecture, drove out its prefect Yang Maoshi and seized it, styled himself defense commissioner, gathered fugitives and outlaws, and his army grew ever stronger; Shouliang could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian took the advice. He rallied eight thousand men from the hill chiefs of the stream valleys, descended the Jialing River, and struck Langzhou. He drove out Prefect Yang Maoshi, seized the prefecture, and styled himself defense commissioner. Outlaws flocked to him; his army swelled; Shouliang could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 部將張虔裕說建曰：「公乘天子微弱，專據方州，若唐室復興，公無種矣。

translations.literal: Staff general Zhang Qianyu urged Jian, saying: "You, sir, exploit the Son of Heaven's weakness and hold a prefecture on your own authority; if the Tang house revives, you and your line will be wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qianyu, one of Jian's generals, warned him: "You are exploiting the emperor's weakness to hold a province by force. If the Tang court ever revives, you and your kin will be exterminated.

sentences.zh: 宜遣使奉表天子，杖大義以行師，蔑不濟矣。

translations.literal: You ought to send envoys to submit a memorial to the Son of Heaven and march under the banner of righteous cause—nothing would fail to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to pay homage to the emperor and march under the banner of the dynasty's cause—then nothing can stand against you.

sentences.zh: 」部將綦毋諫復說建養士愛民，以觀天下之變，建皆從之。

translations.literal: " Staff general Qiwu Jian again urged Jian to nurture soldiers and cherish the people, to watch how affairs under Heaven would change; Jian followed all of this.
translations.idiomatic: " General Qiwu Jian also urged Jian to treat his troops well and care for the people while watching how the world turned. Jian took all their advice.

sentences.zh: 庠、虔裕、諫，皆許州人也。

translations.literal: Xiang, Qianyu, and Jian were all men of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, Qianyu, and Jian were all from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，建與東川節度使顧彥朗俱在神策軍，同討賊。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jian and Dongchuan military governor Gu Yanslang had both been in the Shence Army and had campaigned against the rebels together.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jian and Gu Yanslang, military governor of Dongchuan, had both served in the Shence Army and fought the rebels together.

sentences.zh: 建既據閬州，彥朗畏其侵暴，數遣使問遺，饋以軍食，建由是不犯東川。

translations.literal: Once Jian held Lang Prefecture, Yanslang feared his aggression and repeatedly sent envoys with inquiries and gifts, providing army provisions; Jian therefore did not encroach on Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jian seized Langzhou, Yanslang feared he would strike eastward and sent envoys again and again with gifts and grain for his army. Jian did not molest Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 初，周寶聞淮南六合鎮遏使徐約兵精，誘之使擊蘇州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhou Bao heard that Xu Yue, the suppressor-commissioner of Liuhe in Huainan, had crack troops; he lured him into attacking Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhou Bao had heard that Xu Yue, suppressor-commissioner of Liuhe in Huainan, commanded elite troops, and he incited Xu to attack Suzhou.
